             Version 0.8 2026-07-12 · Added · 3 entries
            • FortiAnalyzer
            • FortiADC
            • Backup coverage page

            Changed — operator menu order

            • Appliances moves to Administrator; Schema builds, Build compatibility and Certificate Manager move to Automation; Global Studio joins Administrator; the Fleet group is reordered.
            • A profile that cannot see the new group keeps the entry where it was (Appliances and the API library under Fleet, Studio as its own group), so the reorder takes no page away from anyone.

            Changed — the FortiADC schema adapter is verified on a lab box

            SATOM's harvest of {device} (FortiADC-VM 7.6.7 build0676) read its CLI tree (527 objects, 3,649 fields), its show full-configuration (315 blocks, no hidden field) and its REST rediscovery sweep (217 endpoints, 7 absent), all read-only. The Schema builds page now lists the FortiADC adapter as verified ({device}, 7.6.7 build0676), and the CLI -> REST path rule as verified: 224 of the 225 REST endpoints the box's sweep read land on a tree object under it, and so do all 19 child tables (<parent>_child_<table>) of its depth capture. Two assumptions were wrong and are corrected in the code and the docs: FortiADC's tree prints the FortiWeb format (CLI ids, types, options), not the FortiOS one; and its REST does not always spell a field the way the CLI does (below). Build compatibility now reads "absent" for a FortiADC object a measured tree does not list, as it already did for FortiWeb.

            Fixed — FortiADC fields read REST only or unknown although both channels had them

            The FortiADC tree of a knowledge pack keys each object by the FortiWeb rule (load-balance/pool), the REST sweep by the FortiADC one (load_balance_pool), and the API library joins the two channels on that key: on 7.6.7, 10 fields of 5,402 read "both" and 862 entries stood for 527 objects (API Versions, Build compatibility, the field map and each appliance's Not-in-GUI page read this). The channel view now re-keys the pack's objects from their CLI path, so each object is one entry with both channels; SATOM's own harvest, keyed by the FortiADC rule already, is the record read when both exist.

            Joining the objects exposed a second difference: FortiADC's REST writes many CLI attributes with _ for - (direct_route_ip for direct-route-ip, 324 fields on 7.6.7), names the table key mkey, and renames some fields outright (pool for load-balance-pool). Read naively, the virtual server's Not-in-GUI section offered load-balance-pool, direct-route-ip and others as CLI-only fields to write over SSH, though the GUI and REST edit them. Now a field both spellings name is one field, shown under the REST name; _nondeletable and _noneditable are REST bookkeeping (meta); and a CLI field REST does not name on an object REST read is "unknown" (shown as unverified on this build), never "CLI only" — on FortiADC "CLI only" now means REST measured the whole object absent (98 objects on 7.6.7, each a 404 at its REST path). FortiADC 7.6.7 now reads 967 fields both, 233 CLI only, 623 REST only, 2,456 unknown, 545 entries.

            Added — every screen in German, French, Italian and Spanish again

            The language catalogues had fallen behind the interface: the screens added since the last translation sweep (about 2,700 strings: Naming Discovery, ADOM Menus, the measured-GUI pages, Software Update, the API library, Settings and most of Fleet) rendered in English for an operator who had chosen another language, because gettext falls back to the English text without a word.

            • All four catalogues now cover every string the interface can show: 6,127 of 6,127 in de, fr, it and es. Spanish stays off in Settings → Languages by default; turning it on now gives a complete interface.
            • A new guard fails the moment a string ships without a translation in one of the four languages, or when a translation drops or invents a placeholder or markup token ({name}, {{ … }}, HTML) — the case pybabel compile does not check. It reads the strings with the same extraction map as pybabel extract, so a new template is covered without editing the guard.
            • satom execute restart-all now compiles the language catalogues first when a .po is newer than its .mo. The compiled files travel in neither git nor an update package; the update runner always compiled them, but a deploy by git pull + restart-all kept the previous revision's catalogues — the primary served catalogues two days older than its code.

            Security — the FortiAnalyzer configuration sync stored device secrets

            • FortiAnalyzer answers every secret as ["ENC", "<blob>"] (HA, SQL and backup passwords, local-certificate passwords, admin-profile data-mask keys). The configuration sync kept them in _config.json and in every stored configuration version, while the FortiAnalyzer pages already hid them. The sync now drops them with the same rule as the pages, as the FortiGate sync already did. Because the blob changes on every read, an unchanged FortiAnalyzer also recorded a new configuration version on every sync; that stops too. Configuration versions recorded before this fix still contain those values.

            Fixed — errors the hourly configuration sync logged every hour

            • FortiADC 7.6.x: the sync asked for every table in the FortiADC registry, including seven that only 8.0 serves (user_app_group, system_sso_admin, …), and logged seven HTTP 404 errors per unit per hour. It now asks only for what the unit's build serves (the API library had already measured those seven as absent on 7.6.7). The API-library harvest still asks for every table: it is what measures absence.
            • FortiAnalyzer: report_generated failed on every sync (-32002 Missing state: it needs a state and a time range). It is the list of reports the box produced, not configuration, so the sync leaves it out, along with logview_logfiles (log-file state), like the other operational endpoints.

            Added — "Not in GUI, but in CLI" on the console, and an alert for stale processes

            • satom get device not-in-gui <device> [--endpoint <key|cli path>] — the per-device inventory of /appliances/<id>/not-in-gui on the console: objects only the CLI serves, CLI-only fields of REST objects, REST fields the Fortinet GUI does not show and objects the device's GUI does not draw, each with the channel SATOM writes it over. Read from the API library and the measured layouts (backend flask not-in-gui inventory); the device is not contacted. Field values and the editor stay on the page.
            • Alert: a process running code older than the disk. The Scheduled automation check now raises a warning (action.code_stale.<web|scheduler|reconciler>) when a SATOM process started before the newest source file and has stayed that way for 15 minutes. On 2026-10-13 the scheduler ran two-day-old code for 45 hours after updates that restarted only the web service; its device sync reported success while skipping the FortiGate the new code supports. Before this, only satom diagnose code and satom get system health said so.

            Fixed — deep-monitor sweep, knowledge lane age, per-device page speed

            • The deep-monitor sweep took 12 minutes on a 3-minute schedule, so every run overlapped the next. 46 HTTPS probes against front ends that did not answer cost 16 s each, one after another: the 10 s request timeout plus a second connection to read the certificate of a host that had just failed to connect. A probe that never got a connection no longer reads the certificate, and the network half of the HTTPS probes runs concurrently (16 at a time). Grading and every database write stay on the sweep's own thread.
            • Software Update named an old API pack for the release lane. When the release's API pack was not imported because a newer knowledge pack already held its content, the lane kept showing the last API pack actually imported (2.6.0 on a 3.0.0 node) and would have turned stale after 30 days. It now names the release's pack, "covered by" the pack that holds it, dated by that pack. Also in satom show knowledge.
            • The per-device "Not in GUI, but in CLI" page took 60 s on a FortiGate. Every object's section re-read the build's whole channel view from the database (80 reads of ~23,000 rows for {device}). The page now reads it once: 1.3 s.
            • The same page counted two FortiWeb bookkeeping keys as fields. Server Policy on 7.6.8 showed 36 REST fields outside the GUI where the policy's own section shows 34: sub_table_id and sub_table_action passed because only the editor applied the FortiWeb noise filter. The page applies it too.
            • satom diagnose code called a freshly restarted service STALE ("0.0 h"). /proc/stat gives the boot time in whole seconds, so a start time read from /proc can be up to a second early, and restart-all right after git pull starts the web service within that second. Both the console check and the new alert allow 5 s.
            • A scheduler restart during a run stopped that action for an hour. systemctl restart satom-scheduler (every deploy) waits 90 s and then kills a run before it can release its lease, and the lease was only reclaimed after the 60-minute TTL — on 2026-10-13 it stopped the deep-monitor sweep that way. A run now records which process holds it (host and pid), and the scheduler releases a lease at once when that process, on the same node, has ended. The run is recorded as failed with "Interrupted: …". Runs of the HA peer and runs opened before this change still wait for the TTL.

            Added — FortiAnalyzer in the live API-library harvest

            • A registered FortiAnalyzer can now be harvested live like FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate: the apilib_harvest scheduled action and the firmware probe (on a build change) queue it, and apilib_harvest.run(<id>) runs it from flask shell. It no longer answers no live harvester for fortianalyzer. On demand, use Schema builds → Harvest: the API Explorer belongs to the FortiWeb ADOM and only offers FortiWeb appliances.
            • The harvest reads the build off the box (get /sys/status), then walks the per-object JSON-RPC syntax (get with option: ["syntax"]) over every /cli/global object the library and the registry name, in one session and with get only — nothing is written to the device. It stores one build-scoped schema evidence row.
            • The evidence is healthy only when the walk read at least one object and no more than a quarter of the asked objects were refused. A walk that read nothing, a refused login, a transport failure mid-walk or a build that cannot be read from the box is stored unhealthy with its reason, the harvest job fails, and the build still needs a harvest.
            • Measured on a FortiAnalyzer-VM64-KVM 7.6.7 build3737 (lab): 165 get requests in 6 s, 139 objects read, 11 absent, none refused, 23 child tables not asked because their parent table has no row; healthy. The FortiAnalyzer adapter is therefore marked verified on Schema builds (it said SATOM's walk had never run against a device), and its evidence no longer lists an unverified reason.

            Fixed — FortiAnalyzer fields read "REST only" or "unknown" in the API library

            • The CLI tree a knowledge pack brings for FortiAnalyzer names an object system/admin.user/dashboard; the syntax walk names the same object cli/global/system/admin/user/{user}/dashboard. The two never met, so on 7.6.7 no field read both: 1,494 read REST only and 1,555 unknown, over 315 entries for 176 objects (Build compatibility and the per-device Not in GUI, but in CLI page read these channels). The library now derives each tree object's JSON-RPC URL from its CLI path and enclosing tables, so both meet: 1,494 both, 61 unknown (children of tables with no row, which the walk cannot ask, and objects the build lacks), 176 entries. Stored evidence is unchanged; other products are unaffected.

            Added — the operator CLI catches up with 3.x: naming, signatures, layouts

            • satom get device naming [<device> [--table <type>]] [--product <p>] — Naming Discovery from the console: per object type, the pattern the device already follows, how many objects follow it, the exceptions with their reason, the types that share {name} through a reference and the Naming scheme pattern of that type with how many objects match it. Without a device: the fleet consensus per product (all agree / devices differ / one device only). It reads the stored configuration tree and runs the application's own analysis as the service account (flask naming discover), so it cannot disagree with the Discovery tab; the device is not contacted. --table takes the key or the label the page shows; an unknown type fails and lists the valid ones.
            • satom get signatures status — the FortiGuard signature DB version and age of every FortiWeb, judged by the same rules as the alert (stale past alerts.signature_max_days, or a device that never downloaded an update), the configured signature source, and what the local signature index holds, with a warning when the index is behind its source's current DB.
            • satom show layouts [<product>] — the measured GUI layouts on the node per product and exact build (configuration, live-monitor and "Not in GUI, but in CLI" pages, the knowledge packs they came from), and whether each managed device has a layout for its exact build (exact / same version / same train / other build / none).
            • satom diagnose config checks the host rule of password-reset links: the node FQDN that replaces a forged or unlisted Host must be a dotted name, LINK_HOSTS entries must be bare host names (an entry with a scheme or a port matches no request), and every name the vhost serves is listed as kept in the link or rewritten.

            Fixed — the operator CLI read the wrong state in two places

            • satom get device status called hourly-synced devices "never synced". It read appliances.last_status, the web console's reachability badge cache, which is written only when someone opens the Appliances list: on a live primary, three devices synced at 07:17 were reported "never synced". The sync column now comes from the source-of-truth store (when the configuration last reached it; a warning past 26 h or never) and the badge is shown apart as the last probe.
            • satom get system health did not look at code freshness. On a live primary the scheduler ran code 45 hours older than the tree, because deploys restarted only the web service, while every unit was active and /healthz answered 200; its hourly device sync reported "6/6 ok" and left the FortiGate out (the old code did not list FortiGate for that action). The roll-up now warns when web, scheduler or reconciler started before the newest source on disk, and names the restart (satom diagnose code has the detail).
            • satom show tree counted the root as a group (44 where the generated reference said 43).

            Changed — Settings → ADOM Menus replaces FAZ Menu: hide the pages SATOM does not draw as configuration, in every ADOM

            • Settings → User Interface → ADOM Menus has one switch per kind of page, named after the page's banner: Hide live-monitor pages (Live monitor: FortiAnalyzer 57, FortiADC 17), Hide pages managed on the device (Managed on the device: FortiAnalyzer 28) and Hide GUI-only pages (no API) (No API on this build (GUI only): FortiAuthenticator 64, FortiADC 17). Each applies to every ADOM and every user: the device menu and the All pages list drop those pages, and a folder left empty goes with them. A page leaves only when every tab is of a hidden kind, so a page with a configuration tab stays. A direct link still opens a hidden page. The panel shows the count per ADOM beside each switch. All off by default.
            • The kind is read per tab. The first cut of this panel read only the page's own monitor flag, which FortiAnalyzer sets and FortiADC does not (FortiADC marks each view), so FortiADC's 17 FortiView monitors stayed in the menu.
            • Removed: Settings → FAZ Menu. It trimmed the curated FortiAnalyzer menu, which a unit with a measured GUI layout no longer draws. Its stored list of hidden entries is gone too, so /faz/m/<item> no longer answers 404 for an entry that list had hidden. The curated menu stays as the fallback for a build with no measured layout.

            Added — Naming Discovery: the convention your devices already follow

            • Administrator → Naming is now in every device ADOM. Its new Discovery tab reads the configuration tree SATOM already holds for a device (no device call) and shows, per object type: the dominant pattern (pol-{adom}-{name}), variants, how many objects follow it, every exception with its reason, and the object types that share the same {name} through a real reference. A part of a name becomes a token only when it equals a field of the same object (or the device's ADOM/VDOM) on at least 80 % of the objects, so {port}/{proto} are read from the object, not guessed from the text — and a name whose port word no longer matches the object's port is reported as a stale name.
            • Vendor objects are counted apart and never shape a pattern: the device's own flag first (FortiWeb can_view, FortiADC _nondeletable, FortiGate q_static/certificate source, FortiAnalyzer protected), then a factory-name list measured on a real unit of each product (app/registry/data/naming_factory.json), then physical port names.
            • Scheme and Discovery list the same object types. The Scheme tab is in every device ADOM and has one entry per object type the product's configuration sync reads — the FortiWeb/FortiADC catalog plus every other table (FortiWeb ~250, FortiADC ~180), including the types no device holds an object of yet. Settings blocks are left out: rows without a name, and an empty endpoint the API library measured as one settings object on the devices' builds (FortiADC firewall connlimit / connlimit6). The FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator configuration syncs also record what each table answered (a list, even an empty one, or one object), so their empty types are judged too. An empty type nothing measured stays listed and says list or settings block not measured; a table keyed by number is listed and says so. Next to each input: the pattern Discovery found on the devices (all devices agree / devices differ), a use it link, and a live count of the existing names that follow what you type. A filter box and Only types with objects on a device keep the list readable.
            • Adopt writes the discovered pattern into that object type's scheme entry. Adopt & adapt opens it in an editor under the row first: change what you need and the count of names that follow updates as you type, then Save to scheme. There is one list of conventions: the separate "adopted" store of the first cut is gone, and anything adopted in it moves into the scheme the first time the page opens.
            • Entries SATOM builds new names from (the FortiWeb catalog, marked builds names) take {name} only (the Managed Certificate its cert tokens): another token would reach the device as literal text, so Adopt and Save refuse it and say why. Every other entry documents a convention and may use any Discovery token ({port}, {proto}, {adom}, {num}, …).
            • Fleet view (all devices: consensus, agree/differ, your scheme pattern) and CSV export (formula-safe).

            Fixed

            • A FortiGate never had a configuration tree. device_sync.snapshot_for sent kind=fortigate to the FortiWeb sweep, which failed every endpoint, so no _config.json, SoT version or cache existed for a FortiGate. A FortiGate sweep now reads every table of the FortiGate ADOM menu at the path the registry resolves for the unit's build (with_meta=1), drops secrets like the section pages, and the scheduled Sync device actions offer FortiGate. Measured on a FortiGate-VM 8.0.1: 344 objects in 9 s, no ENC value in the snapshot.
            • The Naming scheme editor drew an empty catalog for an ADOM whose naming capability was on but which has no naming catalog (FortiAuthenticator on a live install). Every device ADOM's scheme now lists the object types its devices hold.

            Added — FortiAnalyzer joins the measured-GUI engine

            • FortiAnalyzer is the fifth product SATOM draws from measured GUI layouts (knowledge-pack templates per exact build, satom.gui-template/2). Its pages read the device live over JSON-RPC get on the URL the layout names: a /cli/global/... table answers its rows, keyed by the field the table's own syntax names (read once, in the same session); an object answers one object. A table inside a row of another table is read under that REAL row and is read-only. Monitor pages (FortiView, Log View...) say "Live monitor", query nothing and link the page on the device.
            • Writes go through the same audited path as the other products: the dry run shows the exact JSON-RPC request and contacts nothing; apply reads the object first, sends add (create), update (only the attributes sent change) or delete on the object's own URL, records the change and re-reads the object to verify it (-3 afterwards = gone). A password is never shown or sent back (JSON-RPC answers it as ["ENC", ...]); a name with a slash, a table inside a row and the configuration backup are refused before anything is sent; no field goes by SSH (the JSON-RPC URL is the CLI path).
            • Templates are checked against a FortiAnalyzer endpoint grammar on import: /cli/global/system|fmupdate/... anywhere; ADOM data, status reads, monitor trees and GUI routes only where SATOM reads; device actions are cut out of a page (log auto-deletion and firmware-manager timeouts are configuration).
            • The FortiAnalyzer ADOM draws the device's own menu when a layout exists for its build (partials/nav_fortianalyzer.html), and keeps the curated menu as the fallback. "GUI layout not measured" is no longer said once a FortiAnalyzer layout is on the node.
            • The engine reads the templates the harvester actually extracts from a FortiAnalyzer 7.6.7 build3737: endpoints are relative (cli/global/system/admin/user, dvmdb/_meta_fields/device) and are read as their JSON-RPC URL. Views the GUI saves through its own private calls (endpoint_kind django: p/alert/..., p/report/...; gui-api: gui/adoms, gui/sys/advanced-settings) are drawn from their measured layout, read-only, with no Create New, and say the page is managed on the device with a link to it: SATOM never replays those calls. A monitor page links https://<host>:<port> + its measured /ui/... route as-is. "Not in GUI, but in CLI" pages (gui_absent) fill the menu's own group. The importer accepts these templates as measured; the GUI's private calls and ADOM data may stand where the GUI writes (recorded), and only a /cli/global URL is ever sent.

            Fixed — FortiAnalyzer model name and the old FortiAnalyzer pages

            • The firmware probe stored a FortiAnalyzer's model as FortiAnalyzer-FortiAnalyzer-VM64-KVM: /sys/status Platform Full Name already names the product. The product is now added only when the platform does not start with it (FortiAuthenticator's FACVMKVM keeps its prefix). Measured on {device} (7.6.7 build3737).
            • An old curated FortiAnalyzer page (/faz/m/<item>) redirects to the measured GUI page of the device's build when every one of its tabs is drawn there (the requested tab's page, else the first), as /adc/m/ does for FortiADC. A layout's /cli/global/... endpoint is matched to the registry name the old page reads. On {device} (7.6.7 build3737) 12 of the 34 leaves move (Network, Admin, Certificates, Mail Server, Syslog Server, Log Forwarding...); leaves with a monitor, ADOM-data, status or backup tab (Logs, Reports, Incidents, Devices, HA live status, Miscellaneous Settings...) or no tab keep their page, and ?classic=1 still opens it.

            Fixed — FortiAnalyzer schema harvest measured nothing on a real 7.6.7

            • The live schema read asked syntax on /cli/global/system and /cli/global/fmupdate; a real FortiAnalyzer 7.6.7 answers -3 for a branch. It now walks the objects SATOM knows by name (API library and registry) one by one, follows each object's sub-objects, asks a table's children under its first real row, records -3 as absent and any other refusal as not measured, and stops at a request budget.

            Added — FortiADC: every object the GUI does not draw, with its rows, on the per-device page

            • Appliances → device → Not in GUI, but in CLI now lists the whole objects the device serves over REST that no page of its own GUI reads on its build, each with its rows (read from the device when the page opens, read only, secrets never shown) and a link to the page SATOM draws it on. On a lab FortiADC 7.6.7: 46 objects — the 45 of the gui_absent pages of the knowledge pack (VDOM and VDOM links, per-VDOM syslog and FortiAnalyzer, DNS, ISP provinces, connection pool, alert targets…) and Auto Backup, which the build serves but no measured page reads (its GUI tab is an action): this page is now where SATOM shows it. The list is derived from the layouts and the registry, never hard-coded; an object the build answers 404 for is not listed.
            • The device's menu (FortiADC, FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator) ends with a Not in GUI, but in CLI entry that opens this page.

            Fixed — "Not in GUI, but in CLI" no longer treats SATOM's schema pages as the Fortinet GUI

            • The pages of objects the device's GUI does not draw (gui_absent) were read as measured GUI layouts: their section said "GUI layout of FortiADC 7.6.7 (exact)" and the per-device page listed each of them as a layout-measured page. The section now says no page of the device's GUI reads the object, and those objects are listed as whole objects (above) instead.

            Added — FortiADC depth capture in the cache, Analysis and the API library

            • A FortiADC rediscovery with "Capture full depth" now also files its child-table rows in the cache's deep layer, as FortiWeb's depth does: every parent of a child table this build serves (pools, certificate groups, content routing and rewriting, schedule groups…) with the rows read for it, stored as <parent>/<child> under the parent. Where the child table answered rows, the copy the parent embeds is left out, so a pool member is never counted twice.
            • Analysis (Global): the deep-object picker has a "FortiADC object (child tables)" type that opens any captured parent with its members. Sub-element counts include FortiADC child tables, and the fleet inventory counts FortiADC pools and their members as back-ends (IPs and ports included).
            • Analysis (FortiADC): the object inventory counts the 27 …_child_… tables from the depth capture. Before, they read 0 on every device because the sweep never reads them.
            • API library: the child tables the depth pass read are recorded as measured for the build they ran on (verdict and field names), with a rediscovery-depth: origin. That evidence is partial, so on its own it never marks a build as harvested.

            Changed — FortiADC VS Inspector reads only what the virtual servers reach

            • The live VS Inspector now follows references outward from the virtual servers. Each table is read once, child tables are read only for the groups a virtual server actually reaches, and the whole walk uses one reused connection. It used to read about 45 tables and the child table of every group on the box. Measured on a lab FortiADC with 15 virtual servers: 7.6 s and 90 reads before, 0.8 s and 70 reads after; a single virtual server went from 7.8 s to 0.4 s (90 reads to 37). The trees are identical.

            Changed — SQLAlchemy 2 primary-key lookups

            • Every legacy Model.query.get(id) in the application (78 calls across 38 modules) now uses db.session.get(Model, id), the SQLAlchemy 2 form. Behaviour is unchanged (identity-map hit first, None when the row is absent); the test suite no longer drowns in LegacyAPIWarning lines coming from application code.
            • Two handlers that imported db locally after the new lookup (template-binding removal and the managed-WPP lock scope) now use the module-level import, so the lookup can never hit an unbound local.

            Changed — release guards run on the test platform, never on a node

            • The release pipeline's targeted guards and full suite are submitted to the internal test platform for the exact release commit and must report passed; nothing runs pytest on a production node any more (that run cost the primary ~4.9 GB of temporary files per release and competed with the live service). docs/release-pipeline.md describes the new step.

            Fixed — write verification leftovers (policy editor, Create New, FortiAuthenticator rename)

            • The Server Policy editor no longer reads a policy back a second time after saving it: the write's own re-read already refreshed SATOM's copy (the REST part in the write itself, the CLI part in the CLI writer's readback), and the dialog reports that refresh. One request fewer per save, same cached content.
            • Create New (Server Policy) now fails a step the device accepted but does not hold — the re-read must find what was sent, as clone and migrate already require — and undoes that object together with the rest of the run instead of reporting the policy created.
            • FortiAuthenticator: renaming an object SATOM caches by name (user groups, RADIUS clients, RADIUS policies) moves its cached row to the new name instead of keeping the old row beside a new one; deleting it afterwards no longer leaves the old name behind (measured on a lab FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3).

            Fixed — Documentation that still described old behaviour

            • User guide §7.5 and §5: the Server Policy dialog was documented as running only the reference check. It runs the object editor's gates in the same order: the template lock on a template-managed Web Protection Profile, another user's edit lease (an inline-table row is checked against its parent's), the reference check and the build compatibility check; a successful write releases your lease.
            • User guide §28.2, §28.4 and §29.1.4: System Provisioning and baselines render {{ variables }} per device from each template's binding. The note saying they push the body as stored is gone; the preview names a device left without a value, and the live push is refused.
            • User guide §9: the Exceptions page's DRIFT flag (a carve-out whose Server Policy is gone, or uses another profile, on the device) is documented: the banner, the badge, the not on the device filter, and when nothing is flagged. §8.1 adds the Regex Lab button in the measured FortiWeb dialogs.
            • Hypervisor provisioning: config_only (and full) were said to issue the certificate and apply the profile. No mode configures the appliance: the certificate step is a no-op and the profile step only hands over to System Provisioning.
            • FortiGate: the README, docs/fortigate.md, the overview and the user guide called the workspace read-only and said there was no API console. The measured pages save cmdb objects (dry run first, config_write, audited and read back) and the API console sends POST/PUT/DELETE to /api/v2/cmdb/ only, dry-run by default (registry.execute_write). The section pages stay read-only.
            • Site: site/README.md described publication through GitHub Pages and a gh-pages branch; Pages is off and the public site is assembled by its own repository from part of site/. site/index.html, still served by a node's own nginx, named three products and a git source of truth: it now names the five products and the content-addressed configuration history, and the git source-of-truth guard covers it.

            Security — device configurations and database bundles are no longer readable by other local accounts

            The service runs with UMask=0022, so everything it wrote under data/ was 0755/0644: every device configuration in the backup vault (data/backups/<id>/, full appliance configurations with their encrypted secrets and keys) and every system bundle (data/system_backups/, a database dump with password hashes and encrypted device credentials, plus the recovery seal) could be read by any other account on the node — the web server, the mail server, Redis, a monitoring agent. Nothing in data/ is served by nginx, so the directory is closed instead of changing the service umask (which the ACME webroot still needs).

            • data/ is 0750, owned by the service account, whose group has no other members.
            • System bundles are 0600 from creation, in a 0700 directory — written through a private file descriptor, not narrowed after the archive is complete. A bundle fetched back from the off-box backup server is written the same way.
            • The device config vault writes 0600 files in 0700 directories, and narrows a vault directory an older release left open on its next write.
            • satom diagnose data (also part of satom diagnose all) fails when data/ is looser than 0750 or anything under the vault, the bundle store, the ACME account, the recovery seal or the shared PKI is readable by group or other.
            • satom execute repair data --yes applies the rule: data/ to 0750, directories under those trees to 0700 and files to 0600. It only removes permission bits, never follows a link, skips an entry replaced between scan and change, prints its plan without --yes, and is a no-op on a clean node.
            • Existing nodes converge on their own. The update runner runs the same repair after every update, on both the git and the offline-package path. The runner applies its own refresh only from the next update on, so the update that brings this release closes the vault and bundle directories as soon as the application uses them, and data/ itself on the following update — or immediately with sudo satom execute repair data --yes.
            • The installer sets the same modes on a fresh install and narrows what an older release left open on a reinstall.

            Security — fixes from the static-analysis review of the nightly scan

            Every bandit, semgrep and gitleaks finding of the nightly satom-audit scan was reviewed. Most were false positives or accepted by design and are dismissed with a note in satom-audit; these were real:

            • The password-reset link no longer follows a forged Host header. The unauthenticated Forgot password form built the mailed link from the request's Host, which the shipped nginx vhost forwards verbatim, so a request with Host: attacker.example mailed the victim a live reset token pointing at another server. The link keeps the request's host only when it is one of the node's own names or is listed in the new LINK_HOSTS setting (comma-separated, for a public alias in front of the node); any other host is replaced by the node FQDN.
            • The SQL console's CSV export neutralises formulas. Cells written by operators, devices or failed logins (audit usernames) reached the spreadsheet as live formulas. It now uses the same neutralisation as the audit export (shared csv_safe.spreadsheet_safe).
            • System restore refuses link members and uses a real containment test. Bundles come back from the off-box backup host, so they are read as untrusted: only regular files and directories are extracted, containment is Path.is_relative_to (a string prefix let a sibling _restore-12 pass for _restore-1), and the data extraction filter is used where available.
            • A certificate signer no longer runs with HOME=/tmp. It gets its own private per-call directory (or the ACME account directory).
            • The CLI support bundle is private from its first byte: created exclusively, without following links, with mode 0600, instead of being narrowed after it was written.
            • The vault address and the Sentinel model endpoint must be http(s). A file:// address (with # cutting off the fixed suffix) turned either setting into a reader for the node's files.

            Fixed — the documentation generators refuse a source tree without the site rules

            deploy/gen_site_docs.py and deploy/gen_release_notes.py redact this site's node names with the untracked overlay data/publication-rules.local.json. Without it they fell back to the generic rules, and the leak scan, reading the same empty table, still reported "0 leaks": pages generated in a git worktree carried internal node names.

            • Both generators now stop with exit 2 when the overlay is missing from a source tree (one that still carries the adversarial identifier corpus that publication strips). A deployed node and a published mirror are unaffected.
            • The Scout entry of the Fleet menu is hidden for a user without the Scout permission instead of claiming that Scout is switched off for the site.

            Fixed — the nightly satom-audit review is green again

            The nightly full-suite review (satom-audit) had been red for days: 86 failed tests, most of them guards that never followed a refactor, plus a handful of real defects they had been pointing at.

            • FortiGate CPU and memory are measured. FortiGate became an ADOM with no collector and no cpu/memory probe, so a FortiGate was onboarded and never measured while the fleet board offered CPU/memory panels that could only be empty. The Box resources collector and the CPU/memory monitors now read FortiOS GET /api/v2/monitor/system/resource/usage; a missing reading is an error, never 0 %. Verified against a lab FortiGate on FortiOS 8.0.1.
            • The FortiGate ADOM's Analysis page says there is no analysis for FortiGate, and /analysis/data answers 404 for a refused or unmapped ADOM instead of falling through to the FortiWeb WAF analysis.
            • Offline update packages and every rollback recompile the language catalogues. Before, an air-gapped node updated by package kept the translations it was installed with, and a rollback kept the catalogue compiled from the newer release.
            • Werkzeug 3.1.8 → 3.1.9 (CVE-2026-102598 / GHSA-g6x2-hccm-hh4m; it only affects safe_join on Windows, so SATOM on Linux was not exploitable).
            • Booting a FortiADC into its alternate partition no longer wraps a second job around the job it already starts.
            • The web-cache feature toggle no longer names the removed cache_policy endpoint; the Build compatibility page no longer overrides the layout's products global.
            • The FP triage payload field uses the small control of the rest of the modal, and the inspector's Live / From last rediscovery buttons use the product's button style.
            • The node-TLS private-key placeholder is built in the template, so the release secret scanner no longer aborts on it (what the operator sees is unchanged).
            • The API manual's endpoint table lists POST /change-requests/<id>/external-approval.
            • Test guards now check the promise where it lives: the sidebar as it renders in every ADOM (not include counts in base.html), catalogues compiled from the committed .po files (not a node's .mo), field schemas from the shipped API pack plus a fixture tree (not a node's data/field_schemas), and host-independent fixtures for self-update and the upgrade feed. The release-notes picker guards were retired with the Discover panel they tested.

            Fixed — opening a FortiWeb signature profile in the GUI no longer counts as config drift

            The source-of-truth store hashed sub_table_type, sub_table_id and sub_table_action: the echo of the last sub-table edit that FortiWeb carries on the parent row and never prints in show full-configuration. Opening a profile in the GUI flips Table to Main, so an unchanged device minted a version and raised a drift alert. Measured on the live store: 7 of 63 consecutive FortiWeb version pairs differed in nothing else.

            • sot_store.normalise drops those keys at any depth (EDIT_OP_KEYS, now owned by the store and shared with the factory catalog).
            • A new identity rule is no longer a change. record() re-hashes the newest stored body under the current rules; when it matches, the row moves onto the new identity instead of minting a version. Without this the deploy itself would have raised one drift alert for each of the 19 devices whose newest version predates a rule. If the stored body cannot be read, a version is minted as before.
            • The module comment claimed the stored blob keeps every field; it never did (the blob is the canonical body the hash is taken over). Corrected.
            • test_the_menu_entry_is_in_every_admin_block checked base.html for includes that moved into the shared partials/nav_admin.html; it now checks the shared block.

            Fixed — leftovers of the write-verification round

            • The /api proxy forwards the query string. Both proxies (FortiWeb and FortiADC) sent only the URL path, so DELETE …/vserver?mkey=x reached the device as a bare collection DELETE, a ?pkey= child-table read lost its parent, and the write verdict re-read nothing. The query now reaches the device, the verifier and the audit row.
            • Deleting a policy deletes the VIP it owns. The cascade delete kept every system VIP, so deleting a same-box clone left the VIP the clone had created. A VIP is now ref-counted like its virtual server: deleted (after the virtual server that lists it) when no other policy reaches it, kept when one does. Dependencies are now deleted shallowest first (a referrer before what it references): the dependency walk is not deepest-first as the code assumed, so a VIP was tried before its virtual server. An object refused "in use" is retried while a pass still deletes something.
            • "The entry is used." is recognised as a shared object. FortiWeb 7.6.8 refuses deleting an object still referenced with HTTP 500 errcode -23 "The entry is used." (measured on a lab FortiWeb). The cascade's safety net did not know those words and reported such an object as a failed delete; it is now kept as shared.
            • FortiAuthenticator CLI-only settings: one verdict, and it decides. The badge of a CLI-only save came from a second, cruder re-read that could contradict the CLI writer's own read-back (the one that sets the outcome). The verdict is now that read-back: a field the device printed differently is "Not applied: the device kept X (sent Y)", fails the save and is audited config.update.not_applied, like every other verified write.
            • Test guard: in the FortiADC ADOM the Automations entry is drawn greyed with its reason (ADOM menu parity) and must never be a link; the old guard still required it to be absent and was red on main.

            Changed — every write SATOM makes to a FortiWeb, FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator or FortiADC is checked on the device

            The user asked how SATOM knows an apply worked if it never looks at the result, and then asked for the rule to hold for every product and every write path (FortiAnalyzer comes later). Until now "ok" meant only that the device accepted the request.

            • FortiWeb — the verdict decides. An accepted write whose re-read does not show it now FAILS, with the value the device kept, in clone, migrate (the source must read back disabled), bulk, scheduled actions, the object editor and exception injection; "unverified" is reported, never failed. Row counters (sz_*) and the source id a copied sub-table row carries are not compared (measured false positives on a 99-write cross-box clone).
            • FortiWeb — same-box clone. The copy gets its own virtual server and VIP (<name>-<new policy>): FortiWeb refuses the same service twice on one VIP (-7212), a second VIP on one address (-7970) and an interface-address listener (-7637), so such a copy is refused before any write; if the policy itself is refused (e.g. -4, policy limit) its vserver and VIP are deleted again.
            • FortiWeb — every writer keeps the cache in step. CLI writes, file-backed artifact uploads (object and content re-read) and Sentinel's direct writes now update SATOM's copy; the object editor no longer writes the values it sent over the device's copy, and the duplicate re-reads in the row and policy-create routes are gone. Deleting a policy the device does not have answers at once (one read, nothing written). Any job that wrote to a device redraws that device's pages when it ends. Scheduled policy/backend/ certificate actions, which sent a body FortiWeb rejected (HTTP 500), now work.
            • FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator and FortiADC configuration pages. Every create, update, delete and table-row edit is read back and compared; a value the device did not keep fails the save ("Not applied: the device kept comment = 'old' (sent 'new')") and is audited as config.<action>.not_applied. Saves show a badge: Verified on the device, Not applied or Not verified (with the reason). The FortiAuthenticator and FortiADC copies follow the re-read, including FortiADC child-table rows; FortiGate has no SATOM copy and is always read live. Measured on {device} 8.0.3: the device accepts a PATCH of a local user's custom3 and does not keep it.
            • FortiADC writers. Certificate upload/delete, the admin-certificate swap, Lua Studio deploys, the decommission's deletes, the ADC object editor and its virtual-server wizard, and POST /api/v1/adc/rules (new error 502 not_applied) re-read what they touched, keep SATOM's FortiADC copy current and fail on a mismatch. Certificates and Lua scripts are checked by name, never by content. Lua Studio can now actually deploy to FortiADC (it targeted an endpoint no build serves); a FortiWeb target says nothing was pushed instead of reporting a deploy.
            • API consoles. The FortiADC, FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator consoles, the API Explorer and the /api proxy show the same verdict next to the device's unchanged raw reply; the proxy sends it as X-SATOM-Verify headers. Consoles report, they do not fail. Secrets and certificate material are never compared or shown, and the FortiADC reboot/shutdown/partition-swap paths are never read.

            Added — the primary can see, alert on and repair a standby that cannot fetch code from it

            On 2026-10-11 systemd-logind on the primary lost a job; every SSH login of the service account then stayed in logind state opening, the standby's git fetch timed out on every reconciler tick, and the standby stopped converging without anything turning red. The user asked for a way to repair it from the primary, from the GUI or the CLI, documented.

            • HA link card on Software Update & HA (primary): the standby's own state — in sync, N commits behind (measured against the primary's branch head), or cannot fetch from this node since : — plus this node's systemd-logind (service-account logins stuck in opening for over 60 s, or a loginctl that does not answer) and sshd.
            • /healthz/reconciler, a minimal unauthenticated peer probe in the /healthz/backups pattern: decision, commit counts, short shas, time, and a one-line error with URL credentials redacted.
            • Repair HA link (button, user_manage, CSRF-protected, audited) and satom ha check / satom ha repair [--yes]: preview first, then restart systemd-logind on the primary through the privileged runner and show the check before and after. Refused, with the reason, on a standby or a standalone node; the runner re-checks the role against its own PostgreSQL. systemd-logind joins the service allowlist as restart-only and is not drawn on the Services card. Nothing is restarted on the standby.
            • Alert HA link broken (git family) when the standby has been failing to fetch for more than 10 minutes or the login path is wedged — once per incident; it re-arms only after the link is seen healthy.
            • Runbook satom show runbook ha-link and user guide §24.1.

            Fixed — each node's reconciler status is its own, and the reconciler runs the code on disk

            • The status file moved from data/reconciler-status.json to the node-local state/reconciler-status.json. In data/ the data sync replaced the standby's copy with the primary's every five minutes, so the standby's status always named the primary. The Deploy automation card on each node now shows that node's own last tick; the primary-published record is shown separately, labelled.
            • A git fetch that times out is now a fetch-error decision with its error and how long the streak has lasted (fetch_error_since, fetch_failures). Before, the timeout escaped as an exception: the tick died with a traceback in the journal and recorded nothing.
            • Code updates and their rollbacks now try-restart satom-reconciler with the scheduler. Before, the loop kept running the release it was started with.

            Security — the /api proxy no longer reaches FortiADC's side-effect GETs

            On FortiADC a plain GET reboots, shuts down, factory-resets or swaps the boot partition. The ADC console refused those paths, but /api/adc/<id>/proxy/... sent them to the device for anyone with registry.view in the Global ADOM. It now refuses them for every method, before any connection, and audits the refusal (api.proxy.adc_refused). The API Explorer, which is pinned to the FortiWeb ADOM and cannot see a FortiADC today, carries the same refusal (api_explorer.refused) in case that pin moves.

            Added — FortiADC: rediscovery reads every child table over REST, and the virtual-server tree follows every reference

            The user pointed out that FortiADC rediscovery only offered the CLI capture beside the REST sweep, and asked for the same REST depth and the same virtual-server tree that FortiWeb has.

            • Rediscovery → Capture full depth: every child table (REST) is now offered for FortiADC. It reads each of the 27 <parent>_child_<table> tables once per parent object of the sweep. On {device} the members of certificate groups, CA groups and intermediate-CA groups exist only there, so before this the certificate chain behind a virtual server could not be read at all. A table the build does not serve is asked once and recorded as absent; Stop discards the partial capture and keeps the previous one.
            • VS Inspector: each virtual server is drawn to the end of every reference. That covers content routing (with its match conditions) → pool → members → real server and health checks. It also covers client SSL profile → certificate group → certificates → intermediate CA, auth policy → user group → RADIUS / LDAP / local user, WAF sub-profiles, method, persistence, profiles, SNAT and schedule pools. A virtual server with content routing used to show only Content Routing: enable.
            • From last rediscovery draws the same tree from the snapshot and its depth capture without contacting the device.
            • A reference to an object the device does not have is shown as not found on the device instead of being left out.

            Fixed — the FortiADC VS Inspector never showed the client SSL profile

            It looked up client-ssl-profile; the device spells it client_ssl_profile.

            Fixed — a change made from SATOM shows at once, without a rediscovery

            The user reported that enabling or disabling a server policy from the FortiWeb Server Policy list did not update the screen until a later rediscovery picked the change up from the device. They asked for a rediscovery of only the element that changed, as a rule for every action.

            • Every configuration write SATOM makes to a FortiWeb now re-reads the object it touched (or, for a sub-table row, that sub-table), right after the device accepts it, and updates SATOM's copy in every cache layer. A deleted object is removed. The cache takes the value the device returns, not the value that was sent.
            • The rule sits at the single write entry point, so it covers enable, disable, delete, clone, bulk changes, scheduled actions, exception injection and the object editor alike, not only the three screens that refreshed their own writes before.
            • Every accepted write is now verified on the device. The user asked how SATOM can know a change worked without checking it. Until now "ok" meant only that the FortiWeb accepted the request, and some builds accept a write and silently drop a field. The same re-read now compares every field that was sent with what the device holds: verified, not applied (the device accepted it and does not hold it — recorded in the audit log as config.<action>.not_applied) or not verified (the re-read failed, or only secrets or sub-tables were sent, which are not compared). A delete is verified when the device no longer has the object; a new sub-table row when some row carries what was sent.
            • Enable, disable and delete of a server policy now fail when the device did not take the change, with the value the device kept in the error. A delete whose policy is still there stops before touching its dependencies. The job message says "verified on the device", or how many could not be verified.
            • Cost: one read per accepted write (the check), whether or not SATOM holds a copy of the object. A refused write reads nothing. A failed re-read never undoes the write: the row stays as it was until the next ⟳.
            • Server-policy actions (enable/disable, delete, clone, migrate) redraw the page you are on when the job ends, including after a partial failure, because the policies that succeeded did change.

            Changed — every device ADOM draws the FortiWeb menu

            The user asked that the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate ADOMs show every menu and sub-menu entry the FortiWeb ADOM has, each one acting only on that ADOM's own kind of device, with permissions still applied, the Global ADOM left as it is and the device's own menu untouched.

            • Every device ADOM now has the same Fleet › WAF sub-menu, Operations group, Automation, Administrator and Plugins entries as FortiWeb, in the same places.
            • An entry whose page works for that product is a normal link. Newly reachable: FortiADC Device Backups, Migration Report, Firmware (the image vault, needed now that a FortiADC can be upgraded from it), Network Segments and Signatures (the FortiADC signature page); FortiGate Migration Report and Plugins; FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator Plugin Studio.
            • An entry whose page only understands FortiWeb objects is shown greyed out, without a link, and says why on hover (for example "Not available for FortiGate: SATOM has no configuration-backup transport for this product yet"). It never links to FortiWeb configuration from another ADOM.
            • FortiADC Capacity Limits is now greyed out: its catalog counts FortiWeb object types, so the page could only offer FortiWeb rows to a FortiADC.
            • A profile without the permission an entry needs sees neither the link nor the greyed entry.
            • Whether an entry works for a product comes from what SATOM already records for that feature (upgrade flow products, automation catalog, firmware and naming capabilities, Lua targets, backup transports), so the menu follows when a feature gains a product.

            Added — star any left-menu entry into the Bookmarks panel

            The user asked to be able to mark menu and sub-menu entries as favourites with a star, have them appear in the bookmarks bar, and remove them the same way. Every page entry in the left menu now shows a star on hover; clicking it adds the page to Favourites in the Bookmarks panel (as a personal link labelled "Group › Entry"), and clicking the filled star removes it. Stars are per user and per ADOM, like every bookmark.

            • Nothing new is stored: a starred entry is a personal link bookmark with a star, so it goes through the same URL check as any link and only pages of this console are accepted.
            • Unstarring deletes that link while it still sits at the root of the panel; a link you filed into a folder, or a team link, only loses its star.
            • The menu reads its stars from the panel, so a star removed in the panel goes dark in the menu as well.

            Added — FortiADC: Upgrade and Boot Partition on the appliance page

            The user asked that a FortiADC appliance offer the same actions as a FortiWeb. Upgrade and Boot Partition now serve FortiADC through the same runbook (change control, Scout, pre-flight backup and health, reboot monitoring, before/after report, final rediscovery), over the transport the FortiADC GUI itself uses: the image goes to the inactive partition and the box reboots into it. The Boot Partition page of a FortiADC shows both partitions and offers Boot alternate partition — a reboot into the build already installed on the other partition, no image sent — with the emergency-path gates (acknowledgement, typed name, audit) and a refusal before anything is sent when that partition is empty. The pre-flight now reads whether the account may change the system instead of reporting "unknown", and the post-flight runs the FortiADC health battery and virtual-server probes instead of the FortiWeb ones.

            Security — FortiADC GETs that reboot or reset the appliance

            On FortiADC, reboot, shutdown, factory reset and the partition swap are plain GET requests. The FortiADC API console sent any GET for a read-only user, with no dry run and no audit entry. Those paths, plus restore and image upload, are now refused for every method and permission (and audited) in the API console, in scheduled custom REST calls, and in the discovery sweep's endpoint plan.

            Added — Fleet → Architecture: layers, flow trace, autosave, fleet palette

            • Trace a flow: source IP, destination IP, TCP/UDP/ICMP and port. Every FortiGate on the drawn path answers for itself — its routing lookup gives the ingress and egress interface, its own policy-lookup gives the verdict (SATOM never evaluates a rule base) — and the path is drawn in colour from the source host to the destination host: cyan allowed, red denied, amber unknown. Walks several FortiGates in order and stops on the first deny. A public address with no drawn network is the Internet element. TCP traces on a path through a FortiWeb/FortiADC offer Validate with Scout (appliance, hostname and port pre-filled; Scout now takes hostname, port and scheme from the query string too).
            • Layers L2 / L3 / L4 / L7: L2 ports, MAC, speed, link state and VLAN on the firewall links, and the MAC the FortiGate learned (ARP) on each host; L3 addresses, routes and policy flows; L4 services, active sessions and hit counters per policy; L7 FortiWeb server policies (device cache) drawn to the back-ends they publish, plus HTTP probe answers.
            • Same canvas as the Service Diagram: dark network-design view, animated flows, hover lights up everything connected to an element; zoom buttons.
            • Elements from the fleet: the Elements palette lists every appliance the ADOM sees, grouped by product; one click adds it bound to its appliance, with its address.
            • Autosave, undo and redo: every change saves itself; Undo/Redo buttons and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z. Saving is versioned: a save based on a version somebody else replaced answers 409 and the page shows theirs, keeping yours one Undo away. Open pages pick up a colleague's save within 15 s. Read devices can repeat every 30 s.

            Added — Fleet → Architecture: drawn network diagrams with a live overlay

            • New page Fleet → Architecture (/net-architecture/), in every ADOM. Operators draw the path of a service (Internet, LAN, segments/VLANs, FortiGate, FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer, back-end servers, management hosts), link the elements and bind each device element to its SATOM appliance. Drawings are stored (arch_diagrams); saving needs config_write and is audited (netarch.create/save/delete).
            • Read devices reads the bound devices now, read-only and in parallel: FortiGate interfaces and firewall policies with hit count, bytes and last use (and the implicit-deny counter). Each policy is drawn from its source segment to its destination segment through the segments bound to the firewall's interfaces (by interface name, or by the CIDR that holds the port's address); an interface with nothing drawn behind it is reported. Back-end elements with a probe URL get one HTTP GET (status, latency, one header). Nothing read is cached.
            • A drawing with any error is refused whole. A binding to a device the ADOM cannot see, or of the wrong kind, is refused on save; a stored one is drawn but never read or linked from that ADOM.
            • Device elements link to Scout (appliance pre-selected) and Sentinel. Scout now takes appliance_id and policy from the query string as well as the form.

            Fixed — the upload breadcrumbs never reached the log (405 on every page)

            • jobs.js sent its upload breadcrumbs with navigator.sendBeacon, which is always a POST, to /_updiag, which is GET-only on purpose (it never trips CSRF). Every breadcrumb answered 405, the browser console showed an error on every navigation, and the transfer diagnostics were blind. They now go as a keepalive GET, and the navigation breadcrumb is sent only while an upload is in flight (the only time it answers anything).

            Fixed — "Architecture" still named the Service Diagram in two places

            • The Concept Map and the user guide's Fleet tools list still called the Service Diagram "Architecture" after the rename; both now say Service Diagram, and "Architecture" is the new drawing page.

            Added — FortiGate API: endpoint registry and live console

            • The FortiGate ADOM has an API group like the other four ADOMs, and its dashboard has an API console button. The page lists the endpoint registry grouped by the FortiGate menu (every other table under "Other") and runs live calls against a chosen FortiGate.
            • The registry is seeded from a sealed baseline: the 624 cmdb tables {device} (FortiOS 8.0.1) served. Names are the table path flattened (firewall/policy → firewall_policy). Operators can re-point, add or disable entries; a baseline never overwrites their edits.
            • Writes are dry-run by default, as on the FortiAuthenticator console: POST/PUT/DELETE show the exact request and send nothing until Apply is ticked. Applying needs the "Execute write API calls" permission and is audited. Writes reach /api/v2/cmdb/ only (the monitor tree holds device actions such as reboot), and a DELETE on a whole table is refused. An Object key field URL-encodes names such as {ip}/24.
            • Secrets are removed from every answer and from the audited request body.
            • A FortiGate object that is not there (a 404 on …/<table>/<key>) now reads "no such object on the device" instead of blaming the firmware.
            • The FortiGate section pages read each tab at the path the endpoint registry resolves for the box's build, so a table renamed by an upgrade is fixed by a Registry edit. A table the registry does not serve on that build says so, and the device is not asked.

            Changed — one menu order in every ADOM

            • The Fleet and Administrator groups are now one definition shared by every ADOM, so the entries that do not depend on the product sit in the same place everywhere. Entries that do (WAF, Firmware, Naming, Signatures…) appear only in the ADOMs they belong to.
            • Scout is in the Fleet group of every ADOM (FortiWeb used to file it under Operations > Troubleshooting; FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate did not show it). FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate also gain Calendar, Search, DNS Lookup, Fleet Objects and Jobs.
            • Schema builds and Build compatibility moved from the foot of the sidebar into the Fleet group.
            • FortiWeb's API is an API group in the same place as in the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs (it used to be pinned to the foot of the sidebar).
            • The sidebar no longer links Documentation.

            Added — FortiADC: FortiView monitors in the menu

            • The FortiView pages (and Global Resources, Adaptive Learning View) are in the FortiADC menu at their place (knowledge pack kb-20261011.8). They draw live data, not configuration: the page says so and links to the same page on the device.

            Added — FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator: what the crawl could not draw

            • With knowledge pack kb-20261011.7 (harvester 0.9.9) the FortiGate ADOM gains its Not in GUI, but in CLI group (the 540 objects of 8.0.1 no page of its GUI edits), and the pages the crawl could not bind get the objects they edit, with forms from the device's REST schema: Log Settings (syslog, disk, memory, null device, event filter, report settings), VPN Tunnels (phase 1 / phase 2), Agentless VPN Settings, DNS Servers, Explicit Proxy and more. System > Certificates now stands for the local certificates and CAs it lists.
            • FortiAuthenticator pages gain the REST resources the crawl could not tie (TACACS+ clients and policies, RADIUS policy memberships, remote LDAP / RADIUS users, FortiTokens, MAC groups, user certificates, SCEP requests, SNMP); each says it was placed by its page's name. Status objects are read-only.
            • A FortiWeb sub-table listed on its own page (Firewall Admin Policy's match list) counts as where its parent object lives.

            Added — FortiWeb: every object of the build has a page

            • With knowledge pack kb-20261011.6 (harvester 0.9.8) the FortiWeb ADOM gains a Not in GUI, but in CLI menu group: every object of the device's build that no page of its GUI edits, with list, edit dialog and dry run (89 objects on 7.6.8, 124 on 8.0.6). The old SATOM menu entries that pointed at them (V-Zone, Policy Route, Local User, Automation, RAID, CAPTCHA…) now move there.
            • Feature Visibility, Fabric Connectors and External Connector, which the GUI draws with its own widgets, get pages at their place in the menu; Operation gains System Settings, Administrators SSO Admin, IP Reputation its policy, Sensitive Data Logging its settings.
            • An old menu entry also moves to a page that draws its object inside a dialog (SNMP communities on the SNMP form, NTP on System Settings) or edits it through the GUI API (Global Log Settings = disk / syslog / alert mail / FortiAnalyzer; Admin Settings = password policy; FortiGuard = update override and schedule, antivirus). A page's own lists keep priority.

            Added — FortiADC: "Not in GUI, but in CLI" in the device menu

            • The objects a FortiADC has that its own GUI does not draw on that build now have pages of their own, in a menu group titled Not in GUI, but in CLI (knowledge pack kb-20261011.5, harvester 0.9.7). On 7.6.7: VDOM and VDOM links, per-VDOM syslog and FortiAnalyzer, the alert e-mail / SNMP trap / syslog / webhook targets, DNS, connection pool, the old Bot Detection and more — 45 objects in 12 pages. Absence is measured: the crawl opened every menu entry and recorded every read. Each page says so above its list.
            • An old FortiADC menu entry no longer waits for an object the device's build does not serve (the registry's sweep evidence: App Portal, SSO admin and three more are FortiADC 8.0 objects a 7.6.7 answers 404 for); it moves to the measured page of what the build has.

            Added — FortiADC: child tables are edited from the measured pages

            • Create New, Edit and Delete row on a FortiADC child table (pool members, BFD interfaces, HA monitor lists…) now write the row under its parent object (POST|PUT|DELETE /api/<parent>_child_<table>?pkey=<parent>), as the classic ADC editor does: a dry run first, then the write, the change record, the audit entry and a re-read. A child table posted as an object of its own is refused (the row would land under no parent).
            • A settings object that has no fields of its own (BFD, Connection Limit) now counts as drawn by the page that lists its child table, so its old menu entry moves there.
            • With knowledge pack kb-20261011.3 (harvester 0.9.5) the FortiADC pages bind Routing › OSPF's settings to router_ospf (they were drawn over the area table), split System Time into its manual and NTP objects, name GLB Host's collection, and add High Availability › Configuration, Security Fabric › Automation and External Connectors, built from the device's schema.

            Changed — Server Policy: one list, with its actions on it

            • Clone, Clone to, Migrate to, Enable, Disable and Delete run on the Server Policy list itself. They used to send you to SATOM's classic policy list (?classic=1&act=…) to open the dialog there. The dialog, its preview and its job are unchanged; it now opens over the list you are on.
            • Several policies at once: the list has a checkbox per row (and one for every visible row); the six actions run on every ticked policy in one dialog and one bulk run. Edit opens exactly one.
            • The classic list's filters (VIP / IP, backend pool, backend server IP, certificate type, status, /regex/ on the name) and the clone history badge moved onto the list.
            • The classic SATOM list is gone. /web/workspace/<id> now opens the Server Policy list, keeping an act/policy deep link. On a node with no knowledge pack yet the list draws FortiWeb 7.6's default columns instead of falling back to the old page; Create New and Edit then open SATOM's policy form and view.

            Fixed — The Server Policy dialog saves through the same gates as the object editor

            • The dialog's save skipped three gates the object editor applies: the template lock, the edit lease and the build compatibility check. The dialog allow-lists the Web Protection Profile collection (its pencil opens the profile), so a template-managed profile could be edited from a policy and drift from its template on that device. It now refuses a template-managed profile (403), another user's lease (409, nothing sent), a value this exact build rejects (409 on the real write; the preview carries the report), and strips the fields the build lacks instead of losing them behind a 200. A successful write releases the caller's lease, as the editor does.
            • The review table's Channel column read cli_fields, which only the dialog's own save returned: fields of a bound object, saved through the object editor, were always listed as REST. Every save route now names its CLI fields, and the table keys them like the dialog's rows.

            Fixed — System Provisioning and baselines render {{ variables }} per device

            • A System Provisioning profile or a baseline template with a {{ variable }} was pushed as written: the literal placeholder reached every device. Both now render each device's body from its binding, as the template Apply and the approval rollout already did. In a baseline each composing template takes the variables of its own binding. The preview shows the rendered values and says up front when a device has no value; the live deploy (and the canary) is then refused with the device and variable named.

            Fixed — Measured pages: Signatures count, dashboard links, Regex Lab, carve-out drift

            • Signatures: Main Class Enabled Count was always empty — FortiWeb computes it and the REST API has no such field. It is now counted from the set's cached main-class rows (status enable), measured equal to what the device's own list shows. A set whose rows are not cached, or are cached with a different number of rows than the set reports, stays empty: never a guessed 0.
            • FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator dashboards: each card links to the measured page that draws its item, instead of to the old menu URL that redirected there; an item no measured page covers still opens the classic page.
            • Regex Lab (the .* calculator) is offered in the measured FortiWeb dialogs on the same fields as the classic forms.
            • Exceptions: a carve-out whose Server Policy is gone, or now uses another Web Protection Profile on the device (changed outside SATOM, where the re-bind hooks never ran), is flagged DRIFT, counted in a banner and filterable ("not on the device"). Nothing is flagged when the device's policy list could not be read.

            Changed — A page layout with one action tab imports without that tab (FortiADC System > Settings)

            • A knowledge-pack page layout that names a device action used to be refused whole. FortiADC 7.6.7 System > Settings was lost that way: Basic, System Time, Services and Sync List are configuration, but its Backup & Restore tab writes system_auto_backup, which ships the configuration off the device. The importer now cuts out the dialog that names the action and every view that opens it, imports the rest, and says so ("imported without what names an action endpoint …"; the stored layout records what was cut under _import.pruned). The cut endpoint never reaches SATOM.
            • Still refused whole: a page whose own endpoint is an action, a page with no view left (FortiAuthenticator Scheduled Backups — its only list opens the dialog that posts the backup; FortiADC System > Debug), and any grammar break (an unknown prefix, ../): those point at a broken or tampered pack, not at one tab.

            Changed — The FortiADC ADOM draws only the device's own menu; 23 FortiADC page layouts were refused on import

            • The hand-made FortiADC menu leaves the sidebar, as it did for FortiWeb, FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator. The device group, built from the GUI layouts measured on its build, is the only device menu. An old /adc/m/<item> URL redirects to the measured page drawing the same collections (?classic=1 keeps the old page; a leaf no measured page covers still renders). With no device, or no layout for its build, the FortiADC group keeps SATOM's own Signatures overview.
            • The Virtual Server wizard (virtual server, pool and members in one dry-run-first flow) was linked only from the old Virtual Server page: the measured Virtual Server list now has a Wizard button.
            • Layouts refused on import. The knowledge pack carries 101 FortiADC 7.6.7 page layouts; 23 were refused as "malformed": a page with one tab drawn by a GUI widget (System > Settings > Firmware is the hash route gui:#navigate/Config/system/settings) and two pages whose child tables are named after a field (…_child_client_request_header_erase, …_child_upload_file_type) were read as device actions. The FortiADC grammar accepts the hash route where SATOM reads (never in a write), and a child table is checked for actions by its parent entity only. System > Settings, Health Check, LB Profiles, Input Validation and the log and FortiView pages load; System > Debug is still refused.
            • An old URL moves to a collection's configuration page, never to a FortiView dashboard that also reads it (system_global went to the Threat Map).

            Fixed — Approving a WPP template deployed it to every FortiWeb, ignoring bindings and variables; the signature editor had no way in; CLI-only builds blocked every template apply

            • Approval auto-deploy follows the bindings. Approving a Web Protection Profile template deployed it to every visible FortiWeb whatever the family's device bindings said, and pushed the body without rendering its {{ variables }} — a literal placeholder could reach a device. It now uses the scope the template lock uses: the bound devices whose binding follows this version (a device pinned to another version keeps it), or every FortiWeb when the family has no binding. Bodies are rendered per device, and a device with no value for a variable holds the whole deploy (audited as template.approve.autodeploy.held).
            • Signature editor. SATOM's signature editor (catalog search, per-signature exception, alert-only) was linked only from the classic Web Protection page, which redirects to the device's Signatures list since the classic menus left the ADOMs. The Signatures list now has a Signature editor button for the selected profile.
            • A build measured only by its CLI tree no longer blocks a template apply. The "unmeasured blocks" rule refused every apply to a build with no REST sweep even when its CLI tree answered for every object of the template, and the both-channel check had already validated the fields there. It is a warning now ("REST never measured … its CLI tree did"); a build with no evidence at all still blocks.
            • Concept Map lists Compare templates and Template compatibility matrix.
            • Texts: the "FortiWeb layout" button no longer says read-only (its dialogs save), the FortiGate dashboard header no longer says read-only, the binding variables example uses a documentation address.
            • Tests that still pinned the menus removed on 2026-10-11, the old const declaration and the old managed_wpp_names() signature now pin the current behaviour (they were red in the nightly run).

            Added — FortiADC joins the measured-GUI engine

            FortiADC is the fourth product drawn from measured GUI layouts, next to FortiWeb, FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator (layouts harvested from a lab FortiADC-KVM 7.6.7 build 0676; knowledge snapshot kb-20261011).

            • A FortiADC with a layout for its build draws its own menu; the hand-made FortiADC menu stays the fallback, so the ADOM never ends up empty.
            • Rows are read live from the device's REST API (by build, VDOM aware; no FortiADC config cache for these pages), one object by mkey, settings entities as singletons, child tables read-only. Writes go through the same dry run → apply → change history + audit path as the other products; secrets are never echoed back.
            • "Not in GUI, but in CLI" says "GUI layout not measured" only while no FortiADC layout exists on the node.
            • Clone / Create New on FortiADC pages: a clone no longer keeps the source key, and Create New finds the new object afterwards.

            Documentation — the manual gets screenshots, and eleven user-guide sections catch up with the new screens

            • Screenshots. 20 captures of the current console in the user guide (docs/img/screens/, published to site/docs/img/) and the six tiles of the site's "See it in action" gallery, which had shown "screenshot pending" since August.
