They are taken from a live node and anonymised in the page before the capture (device and node names, private addresses, host names, serials, MACs, user names), then the rendered text is re-checked against the real identifiers and a capture with a hit is discarded: the published-docs leak scanner reads text and cannot see inside an image. gen_site_docs.py now publishes docs/img/** byte for byte and removes images whose source is gone; test_site_links.py now also fails on an <img src> that does not resolve.
            • User guide — rewritten where the screens changed: §3 (each FortiWeb, FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator ADOM draws the device's own menu; no Classic view), §5–§7 (Server Policy and object pages in the device's GUI layout, how a save travels, "Not in GUI, but in CLI"), §8, §9, §13 (Fleet → WAF: Search Attack ID, Exceptions & Signature, WAF Artifacts), §17 (FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator pages write, dry run first), §21 (the certificate and profile steps of a provisioning run), §28–§29 (Compare templates, the compatibility matrix, Adapt to firmware decisions, bindings, what blocks an apply).
            • Other documents — stale statements corrected in README.md, fortigate.md, fortiauthenticator.md, wpp_exceptions.md, web_protection_profile.md, build-compatibility.md and source-of-truth-spec.md (device-config history is the local SoT store, not git, since 2026-08-05; where the WAF tools live now; unmeasured builds block a template apply).
            • Site gallery captions updated: "Device sync — git-versioned source of truth" became "Metrics" (the git source of truth was retired), and "Four-copy backup coverage" became the coverage table it is.

            Fixed — Template compare and matrix pages printed a Python method as the product name; the matrix took 40 s

            Found while taking the documentation screenshots, not by a test:

            • <built-in method title of str object at 0x…> in the top bar and footer of Compare templates and Template compatibility matrix, with an empty ADOM badge and a broken product icon. Both views passed product=<str> to the template, shadowing the product object base.html reads. Neither template used it. tests/test_render_no_product_shadow.py now fails if any view passes product= to a template again (AST scan over app/).
            • Template compatibility matrix: 40-50 s → about 2 s for 6 templates × 3 builds. Every cell re-read the whole firmware build twice (the joined REST/CLI view and the CLI tree): 67 + 67 whole-build reads for 3 builds. api_library.channel_memo() shares those reads for the duration of one matrix; it is opt-in and scoped, so a request that ingests and then reads is never answered from a view older than its own write. Same cells, same text.
            • Not in GUI, but in CLI (per-device page): the title ran off the right edge behind the bookmark button. The page now uses the standard header (breadcrumb + title).
            • Template Library: the Note column had no minimum width; since the fifth action button (Compare) it collapsed to a few characters per line and every row grew to ten lines. It keeps 200 px now.

            Fixed — Phone layout: the menu stops working after one navigation, the header runs off-screen, pages wider than the phone

            Operator report: on a phone the menu stops working and tables do not fit. Measured in a 390px-wide browser against a1, not guessed:

            • Menu (and much more) dead after the first navigation. Turbo Drive re-executes the scripts in <body> on every visit. main.js declared const StatusPoller and api.js const csrfToken at the top level; the second declaration is a SyntaxError raised before the file's first line runs, so from the first navigation on all of main.js was dead: the sidebar button, the data-fw-confirm dialogs on destructive actions, tr[data-href] row links, auto-submit selects, copy buttons. Desktop was affected too. Both files now declare nothing lexical at the top level; the pollers are reused across visits (their intervals no longer stack, and an auto-refresh countdown started on one page no longer reloads the next). api.js reads the CSRF token when the request is made — its global csrfToken also collided with the API Explorer page's function csrfToken().
            • Sidebar toggle bound once. It looks the button and sidebar up when the tap arrives instead of holding the ones from the first page. On a phone a tap outside the open menu, a tap on the dimmed page behind it, or Escape closes it. Closing it on a phone no longer writes the desktop "collapsed" flag (the next desktop visit from that browser opened with the sidebar hidden).
            • Five templates broke the same way on the second visit to the same page (Server Policy detail and New, Exceptions, section configuration, Server Objects overview): their top-level const/let are now var.
            • Topbar on a phone: 260px of controls (product switch, tools, search, notifications, user menu with logout) ran off the right edge. The ADOM badge drops its "ADOM:" prefix and truncates its name, the environment and HA badges keep only their icon, the device button is hidden (the sidebar keeps " · change"), and below 420px the logo gives way to the ADOM name.
            • Pages wider than the phone: page-header button rows did not wrap, so one row widened the whole page (Server Policies 865px, Deep monitors 541px) and the browser zoomed every card out. Flex rows in the content wrap on a phone (.flex-nowrap still opts out), and a bare table that overflows the screen with no scrolling container (Monitoring → Collection, System Backup, Software Update, High Availability) is put in its own horizontal scroll box.
            • Guard: tests/test_turbo_body_scripts.py.

            Changed — FortiWeb, FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs draw only the device's own menu

            Operator request: the old SATOM menus are gone from these three ADOMs. The device group (FortiWeb / FortiGate / FortiAuthenticator), built from the measured GUI layouts of the device's firmware, is now the only device menu.

            • FortiWeb: the Loadbalancer (Server Objects), WAF (Web Protection Profile, Web Protection, the protection areas) and Configuration groups are no longer drawn. With no device picked, or no measured layout for it yet (no knowledge pack imported), the FortiWeb group keeps one entry, Server Policy: the device's layout view, else the device picker.
            • FortiGate / FortiAuthenticator: the old fgt_menu / fac_menu groups are no longer drawn.
            • The Classic view button is gone from every list and settings page.
            • Collections no measured page draws yet have no sidebar entry any more: 64 on {device} / {device} (2 Server Objects, 9 WAF, 53 Configuration), 9 on {device}, 26 on {device}. They return as their pages are crawled.
            • Unchanged: the old URLs still redirect to the new page that draws the same collection, and ?classic=1 still opens the old page — the Server Policy Clone / Clone to / Migrate to / Delete dialogs run there. FortiADC and FortiAnalyzer keep their menus: no device GUI has been measured for them.
            • Removed with the menus: the sidebar filters in services.gui_classic (filter_groups, filter_sections, filter_product_groups, classic_url, classic_item_url) and the per-request build of the old menus in the context processor.
            • Guards: tests/test_fwgui_satom_tools.py (FortiWeb list and settings page: no old group, no old link, no Classic view), tests/test_gui_products.py (FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator), tests/test_server_objects_menu.py (no old endpoint in base.html), tests/test_gui_template.py (Server Policy in the FortiWeb group, with and without a device).

            Changed — FortiWeb ADOM: Search Attack ID, Exceptions & Signature and WAF Artifacts move to Fleet → WAF

            Operator request: the three device-scoped WAF tools sat in the FortiWeb ADOM's own WAF group, apart from the fleet-wide WAF pages. They now live in the Fleet → WAF submenu, next to Overview / Inventory / Profiles / Coverage / Artifacts / Exceptions. WAF Artifacts keeps its collapsible shape (Object types, Inventory, Device audit). Same URLs and permissions; only the menu location changed.

            • FortiWeb ADOM only. The Global console's Fleet → WAF does not list them: these are FortiWeb-ADOM pages, and a link there would switch the tab's ADOM without saying so.
            • The FortiWeb ADOM's WAF group keeps Web Protection Profile, Web Protection and the protection areas, and is no longer drawn when none of them apply (it would have been a header with nothing under it).
            • Guards: tests/test_waf_fleet.py (rendered sidebar, both ADOMs) and the Artifacts shape guard in tests/test_artifact_wpp.py, now pointed at partials/nav_waf.html.

            Fixed — FortiWeb pages offer the SATOM tools their classic pages had

            The FortiWeb menu replaced the classic Server Objects, Web Protection and Configuration entries, but several SATOM tools stayed behind "Classic view", so an operator on the new pages no longer saw them. Measured on {device} (7.6.8) and {device} (8.0.6) by rendering every FortiWeb page and its classic page side by side: 214 gaps across 107 page views. Each FortiWeb page now carries them:

            • Config template library of the object's section, scoped to the object type on the page (View / Apply to devices with dry-run preview and the compatibility verdict / Clone / Delete / New template) — on every grid and settings page whose classic page had it (~100 page views). The library is a shared partial (section_config/_template_library.html), so the classic section page and the FortiWeb page list the same templates.
            • Settings forms (System Time, DNS, SNMP, HA, Advanced, Config Sync, FortiSandbox, ICAP, FortiGate integration, interface operation, …): Save as template (captured whole, filed under the classic section), Refresh from the device and a Classic view link.
            • Certificates: Import (over the certificate-only SSH session, the only path that works — REST answers -7721) on Local, CA, Intermediate CA and XML certificates; Generate (Certificate Manager) on Local.
            • File-backed objects (XML schema, WSDL, DTD, JSON schema, OpenAPI): Upload to SATOM's artifact store and Stored copies.
            • Create New through the SATOM editor where FortiWeb's layout has none but the classic page did (CA Group, CRL, admin replacement messages); never for certificates REST cannot create or for file-backed objects.
            • Web Protection Profiles: the Hide default profiles filter (same per-user preference as the classic page) and the Factory catalog link.
            • Server Policy (FortiWeb layout): Enable / Disable (same dry-run dialog as Clone / Migrate / Delete), From a line profile, and Refresh, which now returns to the FortiWeb list.
            • A template saved from a FortiWeb page is filed under the section the classic page lists (gui_classic.classic_leaf), so it shows in the same library.

            Added — FortiWeb templates across firmware builds and devices: compare, matrix, bindings

            • Provisioning → Compare templates (/provisioning/compare): the template a device has against a newer one (the next version, the version adapted from it, or any template of the same kind), on a firmware build or on one device's running build. It shows the field-by-field difference and a verdict: VALID only when the newer template fits that build (nothing discarded, renamed, absent or unmeasured), decides every field the build adds and, on a device, has a value for each of its variables. Approval is reported apart (a valid pending version can go to one device, not to the fleet). Read-only; also as JSON (?format=json). Linked from System Provisioning, the Template Library and every row of both.
            • Compatibility matrix (/templates/matrix): every template of the ADOM against every measured or fleet build (plus a target being considered): fits / adapt / unmeasured / blocked per cell; a cell opens the comparison.
            • Device bindings: a template stays the shared intent of its ADOM and a device is BOUND to it (following the newest approved version or pinned to one), with its own values for the body's {{ variable }} placeholders. The apply renders the body per device and refuses a device whose binding leaves a variable unset (no override: there is no value to write). A binding cannot cross ADOMs.
            • "Adapt to firmware" decides the new fields. The fields a newer build adds over the template's own build are listed in the preview and each one must be decided (keep the device default or set a value); the decisions are stored with the new version (templates.field_decisions) and set values are written into its body. An apply to a newer build with undecided fields warns with their names.
            • Recording the firmware of a legacy template (Template Library → View → "Find the build it fits"): every measured build, best fit first; the build is recorded as authored only when the body fits it. The six templates on the primary were stamped this way (see below).
            • Upgrade pre-flight checks the templates that govern the device against the target build and grades them: a template that does not fit fails the pre-flight (adapting it is the only way to turn it green).
            • The FortiWeb pages offer the SATOM tools again (they were reachable only through "Classic view"): a template-managed Web Protection Profile shows a lock badge and its Delete is disabled; Deep clone (profile + referenced objects) and Save as template on Web Protection Profiles; Save as template on configuration objects; Clone / Clone to / Migrate to / Delete on the Server Policy list open the SATOM dialog of the selected policy.

            Changed — a build without evidence blocks a template apply

            • A target build with no evidence in the API library (unmeasured), and a device that reports no firmware, now BLOCK the template apply (an approver may still override with a reason, audited). They used to pass as a warning, which turned "unknown" into "accepted" by omission. A build whose endpoint is served but whose fields were never read (blind) still warns.
            • The template lock of an approved Web Protection Profile follows its bindings: without bindings it locks the profile on every FortiWeb of the ADOM (as before); with bindings, only on the bound devices. The lock no longer reaches devices of another ADOM.

            Fixed — System Provisioning's NTP element wrote the GUI's own API

            • The "NTP / time" element of System Provisioning wrote system/maintenance.systemtime — FortiWeb's GUI API, not cmdb, with the GUI's field names (mode, ntpServer, daylightSaving). No build has evidence for it and SATOM's GUI layer treats it as read-only, so every profile using it was refused by the firmware check (now that "no evidence" blocks) or, before, pushed blind. The element is now NTP on cmdb/system/ntp (ntpsync, syncinterval; servers are system/ntp/ntpserver rows; time zone and DST are Global settings), measured on 7.6.8 and 8.0.6. A guard pins that every provisioning element writes a cmdb endpoint.
            • "Adapt to firmware" refuses to store a value for a new field that is a secret (jwt-token-secret appears on 8.0.6): a template never stores secrets; only "keep the device default" is offered for it.

            Fixed — the CLI writer speaks FortiAuthenticator's CLI

            • A FortiAuthenticator CLI write never got past config: the writer waited for a FortiOS prompt (host (ctx) #). Measured on {device} (FACVMKVM 8.0.3 build0099, 2026-10-10): the prompt is > at the root and (<context>): inside; abort in a row leaves the row and its table; a singleton (system dns) has no abort ("No such command.") and applies each set as typed (closing the session without end left the value changed; the lab value was restored and read back). The FAC dialect now reads its own prompt, treats "No such command." as an error, and on a failure inside a singleton leaves with end and says the earlier lines were applied (never "nothing applied"). Verified on {device}: system dns written and read back in a fresh session through the DNS page.

            Added — the real FortiGate 8.0.1 and FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 GUI templates render, edit and save

            • The harvester's real crawls (FortiGate 8.0.1 build245: 53 pages; FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3 build99: 93 pages) run on the GUI engine. Their format extras are understood:
            • FortiGate dotted key paths into nested objects (ipv6.ip6-mode, http.comfort-interval): read from the nested object, saved inside it (only the changed sub-key is sent), compared field by field on read-back;
            • FortiAuthenticator measured-inverse controls (Disabled = not active): drawn as the negation, saved as the key with the value negated; JSON booleans drawn as the control's on / off and saved as booleans; lists of plain values edited as text and saved as lists;
            • cond_gui (a rule on a control with no API) said in words in the "conditional" hover; readonly controls and structure values drawn read-only; a control with no measured key lists its candidates ("key not measured"); fold: true sections drawn folded (the FAC pages with one answered 500); FortiGate dialog tabs drawn as tab headings;
            • inline tables tied to where their rows are (gui_products.table_source): a field of the object (router/ospf/area), another collection (SNMP communities on the SNMP form), a monitor: list (read-only), or nothing ("the crawl did not tie this table", never drawn as empty);
            • a list view the crawl tied to a settings object (system/ipam) lists the one table field whose rows carry every matched column (IPAM rules); two candidates or none: no rows, and the page says why;
            • FortiAuthenticator cli: objects (DNS, interfaces, static routes) read with show full-configuration over a read-only SSH session and saved through the CLI writer (dry run renders the script; the channel gate of the exact build decides); create / delete of a CLI-only object are not offered;
            • endpoint_evidence.weak shown as "tied by one field", also_endpoints and columns_unknown said on the list (objects listed by their name);
            • Create New of a dialog another tab owns (Zone on Interfaces, Address Group on Addresses) opened and created in the dialog's own endpoint (it was a 404: FortiGate's subtable_dialogs lists them).
            • An inline table row of a FortiGate / FortiAuthenticator object (and a row of a settings object's table) is created, edited and deleted by writing the parent object with the changed row (the other rows kept), with the same dry run -> apply -> re-read -> drift ritual and audit.
            • Clone on FortiGate / FortiAuthenticator lists: the source read from the device, created under the new name (identity, uuid and bookkeeping dropped; secrets are never read, so never copied), dry run first.
            • "Read values over CLI" in "Not in GUI, but in CLI" works on every layout page (FortiWeb, FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator): the button had no handler outside the object editor. Read-only SSH route, secrets never returned; settings forms get the button too.
            • "Not in GUI, but in CLI" on FortiGate / FortiAuthenticator Create New, from the keys the crawl measured for the object (rest_check.rest_keys, FAC per-view not_in_gui); a FAC inverse control and a field's extra controls count as placed.

            Fixed — FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator GUI templates from a pack get FortiWeb's safety rules

            • The knowledge importer filed gui-templates/fortigate and gui-templates/fortiauthenticator items without checking a single endpoint: only FortiWeb's api: paths went through safe_api. Every endpoint of a FortiGate or FortiAuthenticator layout (page, views, dialogs, table fields, write/writes, bind, FAC gui_writes) now follows its product's grammar (gui_products.unsafe_endpoint): FortiGate cmdb paths anywhere, monitor: and gui: only where SATOM reads (a monitor path in a write or bind is an action route); FAC REST resources anywhere, cli: and gui: only where SATOM reads, crawled form posts only as gui: paths; never a path naming a device action (reboot, upgrade, factory, reset, backup, restore, delete, ...) nor FAC's auth/pushauth. A template that breaks one is rejected, as on FortiWeb; a product with no GUI engine is rejected too.
            • A FortiGate / FortiAuthenticator page may be a list with no dialog (FAC's SAML and system template editors were rejected as "no dialogs / list").
            • A page slug .. or .x is no longer a valid template identity (it filed the template outside its product directory).
            • Measured over the real crawls (FortiGate 8.0.1 build245, FAC 8.0.3 build99): 52/53 and 92/93 accepted. Refused: FortiGate FortiTokens (user.tokens: its dialog names cmdb system/device-upgrade and system/federated-upgrade) and FAC Scheduled Backups (gui:/system/scheduled_backup/).

            Added — FortiGate in the live API-library harvest; a platform exception reason

            • A firmware change on a registered FortiGate now queues an apilib_harvest job like FortiWeb, FortiADC and FortiAuthenticator (LIVE_SOURCE fortigate: schema; the apilib_harvest scheduled action covers it too). services.apilib_fgt reads the build from monitor/system/status, then ?action=schema of every cmdb table the library names for that build and the build below it (the global index is 403 to a read-only token), GET only through FortiGateClient (vdom-aware), and ingests a schema document. On demand for one appliance: apilib_harvest.run(<appliance id>).
            • api_library.EXCEPTION_REASONS gains platform: an object the build has but the measured box cannot serve because it is hardware or a platform image. On {device} (FortiGate-VM, 8.0.1 build0245) those tables answer the same bare 400 as a path that does not exist, so the device cannot say it: schema_adapters.fortigate.PLATFORM_TABLES names 51 of the 54 tables the VM could not serve (NPU, modems, hardware switch, FortiWiFi radio, Rugged I/O, DSL/TR-069, chassis SMC, telemetry/voice controllers, AWS/Azure/NSX-T connectors) and the schema evidence carries them as summary.exceptions; they stay error, never absent. Not classified: application/unsanctioned-apps, system/dnp3-proxy, system/iscsi (nothing says they are hardware).

            Fixed — a FortiWeb page from another build's menu no longer shows in the sidebar

            • A device whose own build was crawled showed pages that only another build has, drawn from the nearest layout: {device} (7.6.8) listed MCP, Custom Tracking and File List (8.0.6 pages; its REST answers 500), {device} (8.0.6) listed File Exception, Caching and Scan History. gui_pages.entries now keeps a borrowed page only when the api library measured the device's build serving one of its collections. A build nobody crawled keeps every page (hiding by measurement would empty its menu). Both lab menus: 145 -> 142.
            • Registry: system_admin_certificate_remote (System > Admin > Certificates > Remote); the GUI component declares url=/cmdb/system/admin-certificate.remote, GET 200 on 7.6.8 build1128 and 8.0.6 build116. Baseline resealed (498).

            Fixed — FortiWeb System Time is tied to its REST collections

            • System > Maintenance > System Time was drawn without values: the crawl recorded the GUI API object the page reads (system/maintenance.systemtime), whose path SATOM never reads or writes. The page now edits cmdb system/ntp (Set Time, Sync Interval), with Time Zone and the daylight saving switch saved to system/global (timezone 04, dst enable/disable, as cmdb spells them) and the NTP server table read from system/ntp/ntpserver (the 8.0.6 crawl had tied it to system/admin). Measured on {device} (7.6.8) and {device} (8.0.6); a write of every field was applied, read back from the device and reverted on both.
            • The device clock is shown read-only through one GET on a path listed in code (gui_bound.READ_ONLY_API); no save route accepts it.
            • gui_endpoint_alias.json page entries take per-field corrections (fields: match by key / label / kind and position; set, drop, or pad the choice values to the cmdb spelling); a bind to the collection the view now edits is dropped, the field is saved with its object.
            • Radio groups the crawl read as one text ("NTP\nManual settings" on both choices; 83 groups on 38 pages) are split by position, in the form and in the grid cells; nothing is guessed when the line count differs.
            • "Not in GUI, but in CLI" judged pages tied by the alias table on the raw crawl and listed fields the page shows (Set Time and Sync Interval); it now reads the page as SATOM draws it.

            Added — FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator get the FortiWeb GUI engine

            • The measured-GUI pages (/workspace/<id>/fwgui/..., same URL names) now draw FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator layouts (satom.gui-template/1, per exact build from the knowledge packs; exact build, else the nearest, with the banner). services.gui_products holds what differs per product: FortiGate rows are read live from cmdb (vdom aware; SATOM keeps no FortiGate config cache) and named by q_origin_key / policyid; FortiAuthenticator rows come from the SATOM cache, else live, and are addressed by their detail URL key (resource_uri; RADIUS clients serve no id). FortiWeb pages keep their own read and write path unchanged.
            • Writes keep the FortiWeb ritual: dry run, review, apply, read back from the device, drift reported field by field; every apply is audited with a ChangeHistory before-snapshot. FortiGate: PUT|POST|DELETE /api/v2/cmdb/<path>[/<mkey>] (new FortiGateClient.write, cmdb paths only); FortiAuthenticator: PATCH|POST|DELETE /api/v1/<res>/[<pk>/], with write-through to the SATOM cache. CLI-only fields go through the CLI writer. A save is accepted only for a collection the device's own measured page edits. Pages with no API (gui:<path>) and fields measured key_from: "gui-only" are drawn read-only and marked "No API on this build (GUI only)"; FortiGate monitor views are read-only.
            • Sidebar: the device's own menu tree from its layouts; the old FortiGate / FortiAuthenticator menu leaves those pages draw leave the sidebar and redirect to them, ?classic=1 keeps the old page. Opening such a page is an ADOM jump to the device's product. "Not in GUI, but in CLI" is on every FortiGate / FortiAuthenticator object, edit and Create New form.
            • firmware_probe reads FortiGate (platform, version and build), so a registered FortiGate resolves its exact build.
            • Verified live on a1 with lab devices (layouts staged for the check and removed afterwards; the measured FortiGate / FortiAuthenticator layouts come with the harvester's packs): {device} (FortiOS 8.0.1 build0245, registered as appliance 37) create / edit / delete of a lab- address read back from the device; {device} a lab user's last name edited, read back and restored. A FortiAuthenticator PATCH of custom1 answered 202 and changed nothing: the page reported it as drift instead of "saved".

            Fixed — FortiWeb pages that read FortiWeb's own GUI API now show and edit their objects

            • About 20 FortiWeb pages (Signatures, OpenAPI File, the XML / TSL CA / Intermediate CA / OCSP certificate lists, Web Vulnerability Scan Policy, FortiSandbox, Automation, FTP Security Profile, DoS Exception Policy, ZTNA Tags, Firewall Admin Policy) were drawn empty and could not be edited: the GUI crawl recorded the collection FortiWeb's GUI reads through its own API (waf/signatures), which cmdb answers 500 and SATOM does not cache, while the same objects live in a cmdb collection (waf/signature).
            • app/registry/data/gui_endpoint_alias.json ties each of them to that collection, measured on {device} (7.6.8) and {device} (8.0.6) with GETs only: the same objects on both sides or every layout key among the build's measured fields (measured), else the twin by name with both sides empty on the lab (named, shown on the page as "tied by name"). GUI keys are renamed to the cmdb keys measured equal row by row (Signatures: alert-only, disabled, exception and FPM counts, custom group, sensitivity); a column FortiWeb computes stays a computed column. Grid, dialog, save path (object editor, audited), sidebar coverage and the "Not in GUI, but in CLI" rule all follow. Verified live: a signature's sensitivity changed through the page on {device}, read back from the device and restored.
            • FortiWeb's predefined Data Types, predefined Global Allow List and the scan history have no cmdb collection: read live through the GUI API (only where the GUI API safety rule allows), read-only, marked live.
            • Four collections the GUI lists were missing from the registry: baseline resealed (+4: dos_prevention_exception, ftp_protection_profile_inline, system_endpoint_control_tags, system_firewall_admin_policy_match_item).
            • A radio or select whose choices the crawl could not read was drawn as a choice "None" that would have saved the text "None" (121 fields). It is now a text input over the current value, marked choices not measured; the harvester (0.8.7) no longer emits such options, and the knowledge pack kb-20261009.5 brings back the real choices of 52 of them.
            • Still unbound, on purpose: System Time and Log Download (the GUI API path is a maintenance action SATOM never touches), Backup & Restore, Caching, File Security and ML API Protection Policy (no collection measured to hold them). Local User and User Group > User Group are not in FortiWeb's own menu on these builds, so their SATOM entries stay in the sidebar.
            • deploy/verify_gui_alias.py <appliance id>... re-measures the table on a device (GETs only). tests/test_gui_alias.py fails if a page keeps the GUI API name, a key or a bind is left behind, a computed column is filled, the table names an unknown collection, a forbidden GUI API path is read, or an unread choice is drawn.

            Changed — FortiWeb pages: FortiWeb's structure inside the SATOM frame, one menu per page

            • Every FortiWeb page drawn from a measured GUI layout (the FortiWeb menu, 145 pages per build, Server Policy included) now wears the SATOM look: breadcrumb with FortiWeb's menu path, page header with the device and its firmware, a card, SATOM's buttons, search box, tabs, table, status pills and save bar. Inside, the structure stays FortiWeb's: its menu, tabs, toolbar actions, columns in their order, dialog sections, fields and live show / hide, per firmware build. Requested by the user: "the style is SATOM's, the structural content is the Forti device's".
            • One menu per page: on a FortiWeb, an old Loadbalancer / WAF / Configuration entry whose collections ALL have a FortiWeb page for the device's firmware leaves the sidebar, and its URL redirects there. An entry with any tab the FortiWeb menu does not draw stays, and so does the Signatures editor. Each FortiWeb page links back with Classic view (?classic=1), where the SATOM tools live: config templates, artifacts, certificate import.
            • The FortiWeb grids gained what the old pages had: Delete and Clone on the selected row (dry run first, then apply, through the object editor's guarded endpoints) and Refresh from the device.
            • An object created or cloned through the object editor is written to the SATOM cache at once; before, it did not show in its list until the next sync.
            • tests/test_gui_classic.py fails if an entry leaves the sidebar while one of its tabs has no FortiWeb page, if ?classic=1 is swallowed, or if a created object is not cached.

            Fixed — FortiWeb dialogs: "Edit entry" opens a stacked panel, not a new window

            • The pencil beside a reference selector (Virtual Server, Server Pool, HTTP Service, …) opened the object editor in a new browser tab. It now opens the selected object in a panel stacked over the dialog, as FortiWeb does and as the SATOM Server Policy page always did: the dialog stays where it was, Esc closes the panel. Applies to every FortiWeb GUI page drawn from a layout. tests/test_gui_pencil_drawer.py fails if the pencil opens a window again.

            Fixed — Create New Server Policy: a service is required up front, and a failed run undoes itself

            • A policy with no HTTP, HTTPS or HTTP/3 service was sent to the device, which refused it (-7715 The service of policy must be selected) after the virtual server, its VIPs and the server pool had already been created. FortiWeb's own dialog marks those selects required and preselects none; SATOM now refuses such a policy before anything is written, the preview included.
            • When any step of a Create New fails, the objects that run created are deleted, newest first (VIP and pool-member rows go with their parent), and the result lists what was undone and anything that could not be. Only what that run created is touched.
            • The New Server Policy form drew 11 fields instead of ~120 on every installation but the first: the field skeleton it is built from lived in the runtime data/ directory, which is never shipped, and a missing file was silently read as empty. It now ships with the code (lab names and addresses replaced by neutral placeholders; the widgets are identical) and a missing file is an error.
            • The scheduled FortiAuthenticator schema harvest skipped its CLI channel even on an appliance with a separate SSH password: no caller handed the password to the adapter. The adapter now takes it from the appliance, and only that one: FortiAuthenticator's REST API key is never sent to the CLI.
            • A policy made with Create New showed its inline tables (HTTP content routing, public IPs) as not in the SATOM cache until the next scheduled deep capture. An applied Create New now starts a deep capture of that device in the background; the policy's page fills in within seconds.
            • Deleting an object removed it from the configuration cache only; its deep capture (a policy with its virtual server and inline tables) stayed, and the pages that read the deep capture first kept drawing it. It is now removed from every cache layer.
            • A knowledge pack's device sweep of a build this node had swept itself was skipped whole, and a node's own sweep reads no sub-table: on FortiWeb 8.0.6 every row field of virtual-server VIPs, HTTP content routing and public IPs stayed unknown (no channel, warnings on every save). The import now adds the endpoints the node never measured and leaves its own measurements untouched.

            Added — every FortiWeb GUI page, drawn the way FortiWeb draws it

            • Until now only Server Policy had FortiWeb's own layout; every other page used SATOM's forms. The harvester now reads the whole GUI of a lab FortiWeb with a headless browser (satom-harvester gui crawl): the real menu tree, every page's grids and tabs, each dialog with its sections, fields, labels, choices and show / hide conditions, inline tables (members, rules) and the dialog their Create New opens, settings pages with no grid (SNMP, Operation, log settings), and the REST key behind each column and field. One layout per page and exact build travels through the knowledge feed, like the Server Policy layout.
            • A new FortiWeb sidebar group mirrors FortiWeb's menu, in its order, for every page with a layout (All pages lists them). Each page draws its grid (tabs when the page has several collections; cell text as FortiWeb shows it, never an internal index), opens a row in the dialog of its variant (an FTP pool in the FTP pool dialog), shows inline tables read from the device as the object editor reads them (not in the SATOM cache when it cannot, never an empty table), and offers Create New with FortiWeb's defaults.
            • Everything stays editable where it is shown: fields, inline-table rows and new objects save through the object editor's endpoints (reference check, build gate, REST / CLI split, dry run first), and every page carries its Not in GUI, but in CLI section — the permanent rule now works on every page with a measured layout, not only Server Policy.
            • Pages FortiWeb draws with its newer shell (Virtual IP, Route, DNS, Automation), dashboards and log viewers have no layout; they keep SATOM's own pages. Server Policy keeps its hand-tuned view, and SATOM's existing pages and menus are unchanged.

            Added — every GUI control tied to the key it writes, measured; log settings with their values

            • Asked: "fields that are not tied should have been found with the harvester so every field is bound; bring those pages in with all their fields; the log values must be there too". About one GUI control in five had no REST key: a label or a grid value can only name a key when exactly one fits, an empty lab collection shows no value at all, and several settings forms do not write cmdb.
            • The harvester now measures it. During the crawl the browser fails every request that is not a plain read before it leaves Chromium (nothing reaches the device), each dialog is saved once into that gate, and the request the GUI tried to send gives the endpoint and every key path it writes; each control is matched to them by its model path, its value, or, when still unbound, by changing it in place and reading the difference off the next caught request. Port and timeout fields are never changed.
            • Settings forms FortiWeb's GUI writes through its own API -- Global and Other Log Settings (POST log/logconfig.*), Admin Settings (PUT system/admin.settings), FortiGuard -- are read live from that same endpoint (SATOM's REST token is accepted there) and saved the way the GUI saves them: the current object with the changed keys set by path, numbers kept as numbers, dry run first, snapshot and audit as for every write. Until now these pages were read from cmdb and drawn empty.
            • A layout can only make SATOM read or write a GUI API configuration object (system|log|waf|server|user|network|router|wvs|policy/...; one rule, the harvester's own, vendored with satom_guikit): any path naming an action (reboot, backup, restore, firmware, license, maintenance, debug...) is never read nor written, and the knowledge importer refuses a layout that names one -- layouts may come from a harvester this node does not run.
            • A control FortiWeb keeps in another endpoint than its dialog (Admin Settings' FortiCloud SSO login lives in system/global) is read from and saved to that endpoint; one Save writes each endpoint in turn and says which were written if one refuses.
            • Fields with several controls keep all of them (Log Type: Event, Attack and Traffic log); the layout used to keep only the first.
            • A GUI API object is sent in the shape the GUI uses, measured per endpoint: wrapped in {"data": ...} (Admin Settings) or bare (the log settings). FortiWeb answers 200 to the other shape and changes nothing -- a re-read after every save reports, key by key, anything the device kept different (drift), so such a save can never pass silently. Verified in the browser on {device}: Other Log Settings 5 -> 6 written, re-read, reverted.
            • A GUI API switch held as a JSON boolean (FortiGuard) is drawn on / off and saved back as a boolean. A field bound to a sub-table of another object is shown, never written (its row needs the parent's key).
            • Coverage after the measured crawl: {device} (7.6.8) 139 pages, 89.8 % of fields tied to a key (713 measured); {device} (8.0.6) 122 pages, 91.1 % (519 measured) -- 84.7 % / 86.0 % before, none measured. Fields nothing could measure in the lab (a reference list empty there) are named from the build's CLI schema only when exactly one field fits.
            • Six collections the FortiWeb GUI edits joined the endpoint registry (baseline resealed): system/overlay-tunnel, system/replacemsg-custom-header (8.0.6), waf/site-publish-helper.keytab_file, waf/site-publish-helper.oauth-spool, waf/site-publish-helper.service-principal-name-pool and waf/waiting-room-custom-page; their pages are now editable.

            Fixed — Server Policy layout view

            • Retry On Cache Size showed its unit (KB (32 - 2048)) twice when editable.
            • The Edit entry pencil FortiWeb draws beside a reference selector is back in the editable view and opens the selected object in the object editor; it follows the selection.
            • Radio groups (Certificate Type: Local | Multi Certificate | Let's Encrypt, Single Server / Server Balance…) are drawn as FortiWeb's segmented button bar instead of radio buttons, read-only and editable alike.

            Added — a separate SSH password per appliance

            • FortiAuthenticator's REST authenticates with an API key that its SSH refuses, so on that product every CLI read and write failed with SSH auth failed. An appliance can now carry an SSH password separate from its API credential (Edit appliance → SSH password, if different from the API credential; blank keeps it, a checkbox removes it). Every SSH session uses it when set and the API credential otherwise, so rows without one behave exactly as before. In vault mode it is stored in the appliance's vault record (field ssh_password) and the column keeps only the vault marker; rotating the API credential keeps it, and the vault migration and local-copy scrub cover it. New nullable column appliances.ssh_password_enc (migration sshpw01).

            Added — One-click GSLB Public IP rows are read and written

            • The FortiWeb registry now lists server-policy/policy/public-ip-list (server_policy_public_ip_item; the REST serves it on 7.6.8 build1128 and 8.0.6 build116) and the deep capture walks it, so the Server Policy layout view draws its rows, opens them in FortiWeb's Public IP dialog, and saves and creates them through the same row save as HTTP Content Routing. A policy that counts Public IP rows (sz_public-ip-list) in a capture taken before this change shows the table as not in the SATOM cache, never as empty, and offers no Create New until the next deep capture reads them.
            • After the first row is written into a sub-table the capture saw empty, the re-read now lands in the SATOM cache too (it was dropped for lack of a sibling row to copy the cache identity from, so the page kept showing an empty table).

            Added — every CLI-only element is editable where it lives, on every product

            • The user's rule: every element only the CLI has must be editable in SATOM, in the page of the object it belongs to, in its "Not in GUI, but in CLI" section. On FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, FortiADC and FortiAnalyzer the section was a read-only table; it is now an editor for users with write permission: each CLI-only field is an input, Read values over CLI fills them over a read-only SSH session, Preview CLI change shows the exact CLI script, and Apply runs it through the CLI writer (one transaction, abort on the first error, read back in a fresh session, audited). A table object asks for the row (the keys the tab read are offered). A write that names a REST field or a field no source measured on the build is refused whole: nothing is sent.
            • Objects only the CLI serves are edited in the same way: on the per-device page (Everything this device has outside the GUI) and, for FortiAuthenticator, inside their own GUI pane — System → Network hosts system interface, system dns and router static; System → Administration hosts system global and system ha.
            • FortiAnalyzer gets a CLI writer dialect (same config/edit/set/end shell). Like FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator and FortiADC it is not verified on a device yet, and the editor says so next to the preview.

            Added — the FortiWeb-layout view edits sub-table rows and creates policies

            • HTTP Content Routing rows open an editable dialog (same save as the object editor's row save: reference check, build gate, REST / CLI split inside the parent policy), and the sub-table's Create New opens a new row with FortiWeb's own defaults. After an applied write the sub-table is re-read from the device into the SATOM cache. One-click GSLB Public IP rows do the same (see below).
            • Create New of a Server Policy is no longer a preview: it shows the POST first, creates the policy, caches it as the device returns it and opens its page.
            • Fields appear and disappear while you edit, as in FortiWeb's GUI: every field and section carries its condition (device facts resolved by SATOM), and the page re-evaluates it on each change with the same tri-state rules the server uses (unknown = shown). A hidden field is not sent.

            Fixed — a save in the object editor refreshes every cached copy

            • write_through.local_update merged an applied change into the FIRST cached row it found; the readers prefer the config layer over the deep one, so the page could keep showing the old value. It now updates every layer that holds the object.

            Fixed — the FortiWeb-layout Server Policy view can edit what it shows

            • The view the sidebar opens for Policy → Server Policy was read-only: a field such as Disable Client-Initiated SSL Renegotiation (ssl-noreg, in Advanced SSL settings) was visible but could not be changed there. For users with write permission, the policy dialog and its sub-dialogs (Advanced SSL…) now edit every field in the place it appears, and so does the "Not in GUI, but in CLI" section under the main dialog.
            • Save shows the change first (dry run, with the channel of each field), then writes it through the same route as the SATOM Server Policy page: REST, or the CLI writer for a field that is CLI-only on the device's build.
            • After a write, SATOM re-reads the policy from the device into its cache (every cached layer), so the page reloads with the device's values and the fields FortiWeb shows or hides for them.
            • Read-only users see the dialog as before.

            Fixed — "Not in GUI, but in CLI" is on every object page, also when empty

            • The section was only rendered when it had fields, so on every FortiWeb object whose GUI layout is not measured yet (everything except Server Policy) it simply did not appear. It is now always rendered, collapsed, with its count and the reason when it is empty: every field is in the Fortinet GUI, no CLI-only field on this build, or the API library has no evidence for the endpoint. Same for the read-only FortiGate / FortiAuthenticator / FortiADC / FortiAnalyzer tabs.
            • The main Server Policy page (Policy → Server Policy → a policy) now carries the section for the policy and for its server pool; before, only the object editor and the "FortiWeb layout" view had it.
            • That page's Save splits fields by channel like the object editor: a field CLI-only on the device's build goes through the CLI writer, the rest by REST.

            Added — GUI layouts per exact build, through the knowledge feed

            • Templates per EXACT build (satom.gui-template/2): the knowledge pack carries a new section gui-templates; each item is the GUI layout of one page measured on one build by the harvester (with Fortinet's labels and help texts), filed under data/gui-templates/<product>/<page>/<version>-<build>.json. A new firmware build no longer needs a SATOM release to get its layout. The importer checks the shape and the exact build and rejects any item carrying GUI bundle code; it does not assume which harvester measured it.
            • Per-device resolution: every FortiWeb-layout page picks the layout of the device's own build (the page passes the full firmware string, build included), then its version, its train, the closest older train. The banner says which build the layout comes from and that it is a knowledge-pack layout.
            • The release ships no layout: the knowledge feed is the only source. A node that has not imported a knowledge pack yet (fresh install, offline, knowledge.fetch_mode=off) has no layout; the sidebar's Server Policy leaf then opens SATOM's own Server Policy list with a notice instead of a 404.
            • GUI changes in reports: the migration report gains a gui block and gui_* rows (a field FortiWeb's GUI no longer shows is a warning, any other change is info), Build compatibility → Compare shows the GUI layout changes, api_library.compare() carries a gui channel, and a bulk apply notes the fields the target build's GUI does not show. Only layouts measured on both builds are compared; otherwise the report says the layout was not measured.
            • app/vendor/satom_guikit/ — the harvester's GUI-template contract (standard library only), vendored and pinned by hash (deploy/vendor_guikit.sh).

            Added — "Not in GUI, but in CLI": every field a device has, on every product

            • Permanent rule: SATOM shows every field a device has on its exact build. The fields the Fortinet GUI does not show are no longer missing or mixed into other groups: they are listed in a section titled "Not in GUI, but in CLI", and each one says how SATOM writes it — REST (a normal save), CLI (the CLI writer over SSH, for fields the API library measured cli_only or hidden on that build) or unverified on this build.
            • FortiWeb object editor: the section in every object and in every sub-table row, editable. A field the REST read did not return shows as an empty text box (never a toggle claiming "disabled"); Read values over CLI fills it from a read-only show full-configuration (secrets are never returned). A sub-table row save now routes its CLI-only fields through the CLI writer inside the parent row; a new row carrying a CLI-only field is refused before any write, with the reason.
            • FortiWeb Server Policy layout view: the REST fields FortiWeb's own GUI does not place (34 on 7.6.8, 39 on 8.0.6 — the five new ones are ssl-ja4, tls-pqc-support, tls-pqc-groups, allow-nonstd-http, unnormalized-url-match) are listed under the main dialog with their values. Toggle groups (Supported SSL Protocols) and list columns (Status, Protocol) count as shown by the GUI.
            • FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer: every table view carries the section for its object; FortiADC and FortiAnalyzer say their GUI layout and CLI tree are not measured (no lab device) — nothing is hidden.
            • Per-device page Appliances → <device> → Not in GUI, but in CLI (/appliances/<id>/not-in-gui): whole objects only the CLI serves (e.g. FortiAuthenticator system dns, system interface, router static) and the CLI-only fields of objects REST serves (FortiGate 8.0.1: 166 fields in 76 tables).

            Added — Server Policy in the FortiWeb GUI layout (read-only)

            • Server Policy → FortiWeb layout: the policy list, the Create New menu and every dialog (HTTP, FTP, ADFS, TCP proxy, Advanced SSL settings, HTTP Content Routing rule, Public IP) drawn the way FortiWeb's own GUI lays them out — same section titles, field order, labels, control types and options, the same default columns per operation mode, and the same fields shown or hidden by the policy's settings, the operation mode and system feature-visibility. Drawn with SATOM's theme; read-only, served from the local cache (no device calls). Routes /workspace/<id>/gui, /workspace/<id>/gui/policy/<name>[?dialog=…] and /workspace/<id>/gui/new/<dialog> (the Create New form with FortiWeb's own defaults, as a preview).
            • Layout templates (schema satom.gui-template/1, delivered by the knowledge feed — see above), extracted from the GUI a FortiWeb serves by satom-harvester gui fetch|extract, never written by hand. The first one is FortiWeb 7.6.x, built from 7.6.8 build1128: 9 dialogs, 186 fields, every field cross-checked against the REST keys of that build. A device on a newer train (8.0.x) gets the 7.6 layout with a warning that newer firmware adds or renames fields; a field whose condition depends on something SATOM cannot read about the device is shown and marked "conditional", never hidden.
            • Inline sub-tables in the policy dialog — HTTP Content Routing and One Click GSLB Public IP — with FortiWeb's toolbar (Create New / Edit / Delete / Move / Search), its default columns and cell formatting (the Server Pool read through the chosen routing policy, an inherited Web Protection Profile left blank). Edit / double-click opens the row in its own dialog (?dialog=http-content-routing&sub=<id>). A sub-table SATOM does not capture yet (Public IP) says so instead of showing an empty grid.
            • Sidebar: Loadbalancer now shows Policy → Server Policy, as in FortiWeb's menu; the leaf opens the FortiWeb layout of the device in context (the device picker when none is selected). The SATOM view stays one click away from the layout page.

            Added — signature source and local signature index

            • Administrator → Signatures → Signature source: choose the FortiWeb SATOM collects signatures from. Save and collect now reads its whole catalog (read-only REST, a background job). The setting is signatures.source.fortiweb.
            • Local signature index: every signature id with its class, description and lineage (first seen, last seen, removed in), a snapshot per database version, and what each version added, changed or removed (new tables signature_snapshots, signature_entries, signature_changes; migration sigidx01_signature_index; content under data/signatures/objects/). A new version notifies every administrator. Snapshot history with a details page and a search over the index on the Signatures page. An empty read is refused; a read equal to the latest snapshot writes nothing.
            • signature_check now reads the database versions over REST (GET /api/v2.0/system/config.fortiguard: signature DB plus antivirus, IP reputation, GeoIP, known bots and the rest, with licence validity), keeping diagnose system update info over SSH as the fallback, and collects the catalog from the source when its version is new. The stale reason names an invalid FortiGuard licence.
            • Alert device.signature_source_missing: FortiWebs registered and no signature source (or a deleted one).

            Changed

            • The signature_sync scheduled action indexes through the signature index and only from the configured source; any other target is refused. Before, any device overwrote the shared catalog, so the cached catalog could belong to whichever box was read last.
            • A failed catalog read from the source makes the signature_check round red; a node with no FortiWeb says so instead of reporting "0 current".

            Fixed — a rediscovery with deep or CLI capture no longer looks finished halfway

            • The REST sweep wrote done the moment its own pass ended, even when the deep capture (WPP + policy graph) or the CLI capture was still to run. done is terminal for the Rediscover page and the Capture card, so both stopped polling at 100 % and never showed the later phases or their end, and Start came back while the deep pass was still reading the box. The sweep now keeps the run live (snapshot saved — starting the deep capture) and only the last phase writes done.
            • A sweep that returns with its state still live is closed as failed with a sentence saying so, instead of leaving the page polling and blocking new runs for 15 minutes.
            • The Rediscover page says Finished at HH:MM:SS UTC in words when the run ends.
